workflow.approveNote.defaultMessage: {becomes, select, decision {Note (optional): also recorded as your decision} reason {Note (optional): the reason for what the agent asked} other {Note (optional): added as your comment}}
workflow.approveNote.description: The label and placeholder of an optional text box beside Approve (For you, the card dialog's merge queue): a note sent with the approval. It says what the note becomes: on an agent's question (decision), one of the card's decisions as well as the user's comment; on a question that offers one action (reason), the reason for that action; on Combwork's own requests (other), the user's comment on the card. Keep the select keys as they are; translate each choice. Glossary: decision.

workflow.contradiction.combworkMergesNee.defaultMessage: Merging needs Git: without version control, work is accepted where it is.
workflow.contradiction.combworkMergesNee.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a merge option was set for a project with no version control.

workflow.contradiction.committedNeedsFol.defaultMessage: “Committed is done” needs everyone in the project folder.
workflow.contradiction.committedNeedsFol.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: “Committed is done” was chosen while each card has its own folder.

workflow.contradiction.focusedNeedsRunne.defaultMessage: Each card’s focused tests need the command that runs them.
workflow.contradiction.focusedNeedsRunne.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved (G20): “Each card’s focused tests” is on but the project has no command to run them (its runner, focused.run).

workflow.contradiction.jjNeedsSlots.defaultMessage: With jj, each card needs its own folder: agents sharing the project folder aren’t supported yet.
workflow.contradiction.jjNeedsSlots.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved (HI-2799): a project using jj (Jujutsu) was set to have everyone work in the project folder. Keep jj (the tool’s name).

workflow.contradiction.jjYouIntegrate.defaultMessage: With jj, you integrate the reviewed work yourself: Combwork doesn’t merge it.
workflow.contradiction.jjYouIntegrate.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved (HI-2799): a project using jj (Jujutsu) had another finish chosen than “You integrate it”. Keep jj (the tool’s name).

workflow.contradiction.mergeNeedsSlots.defaultMessage: When Combwork or the agent merges, each card needs its own folder.
workflow.contradiction.mergeNeedsSlots.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a merging option was chosen while everyone works in the project folder.

workflow.contradiction.noneHasNoSlots.defaultMessage: Without version control, everyone works in the project folder.
workflow.contradiction.noneHasNoSlots.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: separate folders per card were set for a project with no version control.

workflow.contradiction.okWithReview.defaultMessage: Your OK before merging is already part of review by you.
workflow.contradiction.okWithReview.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: the user's OK before merging was set while the user already reviews.

workflow.contradiction.poolNeedsAgent.defaultMessage: A shared pool of reviewers needs review by reviewer agents.
workflow.contradiction.poolNeedsAgent.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: “Reviewers” was set to a shared pool (reviewer agents lanes share) without review by reviewer agents.

workflow.contradiction.quorumNeedsAgent.defaultMessage: Two reviewers per card need review by reviewer agents.
workflow.contradiction.quorumNeedsAgent.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: two reviewers per card were set without reviewer agents.

workflow.contradiction.selfReview.defaultMessage: “Nobody reviews their own work” can't be off while a reviewer agent checks the work.
workflow.contradiction.selfReview.description: Why workflow options in the Version Control tab cannot be saved: the no-self-review option was turned off while a reviewer agent is required.

workflow.contradiction.subfolderTarget.defaultMessage: This project is inside a larger repository: name the branch its work merges into.
workflow.contradiction.subfolderTarget.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved (OP-29): Combwork or the agent merges, but the project is a subfolder of a bigger Git repository and its own options name no target branch (merges would affect the whole repository).

workflow.contradiction.upToDateNeedsSlot.defaultMessage: Slots are brought up to date only when each card has its own folder.
workflow.contradiction.upToDateNeedsSlot.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: “Slots are brought up to date before each card” (G15) was set while everyone works in the project folder (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.forYou.decidedAfterMerge.defaultMessage: {card} was decided after it merged: does it need a follow-up?
workflow.forYou.decidedAfterMerge.description: A For you request (Decide): a decision was recorded on the card while its work was being merged, so the merged work didn't see it. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.focusedSkip.defaultMessage: {card}’s focused tests were skipped at its merge: {tests}. Merge it with them skipped?
workflow.forYou.focusedSkip.description: A For you request (Approve, G20, HI-1367): the merge queue ran the card’s focused tests ({tests}: test names, each with why it was skipped in brackets, as its project’s runner said) and some were skipped for their environment (a usage limit, a sign-in, the network). Approve merges the card with them skipped; Decline returns it. The card’s reviewer agent is asked too.

workflow.forYou.lineAsk.defaultMessage: {line} still has {card}'s work, squashed into {target}: approve and Combwork brings the branch up to date once, or decline and do it yourself before {next} starts.
workflow.forYou.lineAsk.description: A For you request (approve or decline, §16.19.2): Settings → Advanced has Combwork ask before moving an agent's branch after a squash merge. Approving lets Combwork move it this once (git reset --keep, which never overwrites uncommitted work); declining leaves it to the user. {line} a branch name; {card} and {next} card keys like AM-12; {target} the branch merged into.

workflow.forYou.lineRefused.defaultMessage: Git wouldn't bring {line} up to date with {target}: {reason}. {next} starts once the branch is up to date.
workflow.forYou.lineRefused.description: A For you request (Decide, §16.19.2): Combwork tried to move the builder's branch after a squash merge and git refused; the lane waits. {line} a branch name, {target} the branch merged into, {reason} git's own message (English), {next} a card key.

workflow.forYou.lineUnfinished.defaultMessage: Combwork's move of {line} to {to} didn't finish and couldn't be put back. Bring the branch to {target} with its files and index clean, or back where it was: {next} starts once it is settled.
workflow.forYou.lineUnfinished.description: A For you request (Decide, §16.19.2): moving the builder's branch failed part way and Combwork couldn't undo it, so the branch, its files or its index may disagree; the lane waits. {line} a branch name, {to} a short commit id, {target} the branch merged into, {next} a card key.

workflow.forYou.lineWork.defaultMessage: {line} has work that isn't in {target}: {commits}. Decide what happens to it: {next} starts once the branch is up to date.
workflow.forYou.lineWork.description: A For you request (Decide, §16.19.2): the builder's branch has commits that weren't merged (made after the card was approved, say), so Combwork won't move the branch and lose them; the lane waits. {line} a branch name, {target} the branch merged into, {commits} a list of short commit ids with their subjects, {next} a card key.

workflow.forYou.mergeChoice.defaultMessage: How should Combwork merge {project}'s cards into {target}? Choose the merge style and the commit message: until now Combwork made a merge commit with its own message (the card's key and title, with trailers). The merge queue waits for your answer.
workflow.forYou.mergeChoice.description: A For you request (Decide, HI-1697): a project from before 1.0 reached the merge queue for the first time, and nobody chose how its cards are merged, so the queue asks. {project} is a project's name, {target} the branch merged into. Merge style and Commit message are workflow options' names (glossary 2.6): use their words. Trailers: git's “Key: value” lines at a message's end.

workflow.forYou.newDecision.defaultMessage: {card} has a new decision: your review again?
workflow.forYou.newDecision.description: A For you request: the user decided something new on a card in Review, so their review is asked again. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.okBefore.description: A For you request: the card passed review and waits for the user's OK before it merges (glossary 2.3: approval). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.passedReview.description: A For you request: reviewer agents passed the card, and the user reviews after them (A reviewer agent, then you). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.queueAdvance.defaultMessage: {card} is tested and ready to merge: update {target} in {folder} now?
workflow.forYou.queueAdvance.description: A For you request (Approve, §16.9.2): the merge queue has merged and checked the card's work, and waits for the user's OK before it updates the branch {target}, which is checked out in the folder {folder} (its files change there). Settings → Advanced → Merge into a checked-out branch: Ask each time. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.queuePublish.defaultMessage: Combwork pushed {card} ({result}) to {endpoint} for {target}, but never heard whether the push arrived, and {target} there doesn’t show it now. Approve if {result} was published (someone may have removed it since); decline if it wasn’t, and the queue tests {card} again. Until you answer, the queue for {target} waits.
workflow.forYou.queuePublish.description: A For you request (Approve, HI-1183, §16.9.4, “The target branch follows its remote”): the merge queue pushed a merge to the remote, the push’s answer was lost (the network, a crash), and the remote’s branch doesn’t contain it now, so Combwork can’t tell whether it was published and asks. {card} a card key like AM-12; {result} a short commit id; {endpoint} the remote’s address without credentials; {target} the branch.

workflow.forYou.queueStuck.defaultMessage: {card}'s merge into {target} stopped part way in {folder}, with {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} left between the two, and Combwork changes nothing more there. The card's Work section lists each file and its side, and the commands to copy. {how, select, both {To finish it, run {finish} (PowerShell) in {project}; to undo it, run {undo} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} finish {To finish it, run {finish} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} undo {To undo it, run {undo} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} other {Its files are neither as they were nor as merged: put them right by hand.}} Then answer here, and the queue looks again.
workflow.forYou.queueStuck.description: A For you request (Decide, §16.9.2's terminal state): the merge queue was updating the branch {target}, checked out in the folder {folder}, and something (a crash, another program) left it half done, so the merge queue for {target} is paused until the user settles it. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {files} how many files the merge left part way; the card's Work section is a section of the card's dialog (glossary 2.4: work); {project} the project folder; {finish} and {undo} are git commands for PowerShell (keep them exactly, with (PowerShell) after them). Translate each choice of {how}; keep the codes before the braces.

workflow.forYou.review.description: A For you request: the card waits for the user to review it (Version Control → Work is reviewed before it is merged: You). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.roundLimit.defaultMessage: {card} failed {rounds, plural, one {# review} other {# reviews}}: carry on with more rounds, split it, accept it with follow-ups, or take it over?
workflow.forYou.roundLimit.description: A For you request (Decide): the card reached its card loop's round limit (Settings → Card loops), so its loop pauses until the user chooses one of four ways on. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {rounds} the reviews it failed (a number).

workflow.forYou.slotDirty.defaultMessage: {card} is Done, but {slot} has uncommitted changes, so it stays on {line}. Commit or discard them there: Combwork then detaches the slot at {target}, ready for its next card.
workflow.forYou.slotDirty.description: A For you request (Decide, HI-2014): a card reached Done while its slot (a reused working folder, such as slot-b) had uncommitted changes, so Combwork left the slot on the card's branch {line} instead of detaching it at the target branch {target}. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {slot}, {line} and {target} are names, kept as they are.

workflow.forYouKind.defaultMessage: {kind, select, approve {Approve} decide {Decide} test {Test} signIn {Sign in} other {Other}}
workflow.forYouKind.description: The kind of a request for the user (For you), shown as its label: approve something, decide something, test something, sign in somewhere, or anything else. Translate each choice; keep the codes before the braces.

workflow.form.addCheck.description: A button under the checks of “Checks pass before review”.

workflow.form.allOff.description: A choice beside the presets in the Workflow section: every rule off (SPEC §16.6.4).

workflow.form.allOffSummary.defaultMessage: No review, nothing checked, everyone in the project folder: cards move freely, and Combwork still records what happens.
workflow.form.allOffSummary.description: What the choice “All off” sets up, under its name in the Workflow section.

workflow.form.appliesNow.defaultMessage: Only the stage names change: names aren’t rules, so they apply now, to every card.
workflow.form.appliesNow.description: The message of the dialog before saving workflow options when only stage names change (glossary 2.2: stage).

workflow.form.appliesNowBranches.defaultMessage: Only the other branches work can merge into change: they aren’t rules, so they apply now. A lane or card already merging into one keeps it.
workflow.form.appliesNowBranches.description: HI-2556: the message of the dialog before saving workflow options when only “Other branches work can merge into” changes (or that and stage names).

workflow.form.cantSave.description: Above the reasons the workflow options can’t be saved, each a sentence of its own.

workflow.form.carried.defaultMessage: Agents’ old worktrees finish their current work first: {agents}. Then they work in slots too.
workflow.form.carried.description: Under “Where cards are built” (G11) while agents still hold their worktrees from before 1.0 (#1441), kept until their current card or lane ends. {agents} is a list of agent names (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.form.changeLine.description: A line of the list of what changes, in the dialog before saving workflow options: an option’s name, its value now and its new value.

workflow.form.changedMeanwhile.defaultMessage: The workflow options changed meanwhile, so nothing was saved. They’re shown as they are now.
workflow.form.changedMeanwhile.description: A notification: saving the Workflow section was refused because the options changed after it was read (in another window, or by the Combwork Assistant); the section reloads them.

workflow.form.changesHead.description: In the dialog before saving workflow options: above the list of options that change, each with its old and new value.

workflow.form.checkCommand.description: The placeholder of a check’s command field (Project Settings → Workflow → Checks pass before review).

workflow.form.checkName.description: The placeholder of a check’s name field (Project Settings → Workflow → Checks pass before review).

workflow.form.closePreview.description: A button in a preset’s preview: closes it without changing the form.

workflow.form.confirmMessage.defaultMessage: The new options apply from the next card that starts.
workflow.form.confirmMessage.description: The message of the dialog before saving workflow options.

workflow.form.confirmTitle.description: The title of the dialog before saving workflow options.

workflow.form.copied.description: A notification: the workflow options were copied to the clipboard.

workflow.form.copy.description: The button copying the project’s workflow options as JSON, to paste into another project.

workflow.form.defaultBranch.description: The placeholder of the target branch field in Project Settings → Workflow: left empty, the default branch.

workflow.form.discard.description: The button dropping unsaved changes to the workflow options.

workflow.form.fileLocksNote.defaultMessage: Applies to agents working in the same folder, outside a slot.
workflow.form.fileLocksNote.description: Under the workflow option “File locks”: a slot is a folder Combwork lends to a card or its lane (glossary 2.5: slot), so agents in different slots never share a file.

workflow.form.focusedPick.description: The placeholder and label of a field under “Each card’s focused tests” (G20) in Project Settings → Workflow: the project’s command that lists the tests a change needs. Left empty, each card’s builder names its tests.

workflow.form.focusedRun.description: The placeholder and label of a field under “Each card’s focused tests” (G20) in Project Settings → Workflow: the project’s command that runs a list of tests.

workflow.form.folders.defaultMessage: Folders and files, separated by commas
workflow.form.folders.description: The placeholder of the field “What the work is” (folders and files left out).

workflow.form.from.global.description: Where a workflow option’s value comes from: Combwork’s own default.

workflow.form.from.here.description: Where a workflow default’s value comes from, in Settings → Workflow defaults or Settings → Workspace: set at this level.

workflow.form.from.platform.description: Where a workflow option’s value comes from: nobody set it (every rule off).

workflow.form.from.preset.description: Where a workflow option’s value comes from: the preset chosen.

workflow.form.from.project.description: Where a workflow option’s value comes from: set in this project.

workflow.form.from.workspace.description: Where a workflow option’s value comes from: the workspace’s default.

workflow.form.fromTemplateDraft.defaultMessage: Filled in from the template {template}: these options aren’t saved yet. Check them, then Save… (they apply from the next card), or Discard Changes.
workflow.form.fromTemplateDraft.description: A note atop the Workflow section (HI-1910, HI-2083) after loading a template whose workflow was applied and saved nothing of it: its options are filled in but not saved. Save… and Discard Changes are the buttons below: as translated there.

workflow.form.fromTemplateMax.defaultMessage: Filled in from the template {template}. Its Maximum agents ({max, number}) is saved already, with its agents; the other options aren’t saved yet. Check them, then Save… (they apply from the next card), or Discard Changes.
workflow.form.fromTemplateMax.description: A note atop the Workflow section (HI-2083) after loading a template whose workflow was applied: the load saved its Maximum agents ({max}) with its agents (HI-2058), the rest is filled in but not saved. Maximum agents, Save… and Discard Changes are names in the form: as translated there.

workflow.form.heir.description: A project inheriting a change of workflow defaults, in the dialog before saving them: its name, then the options that change for it, as a list.

workflow.form.heirCards.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {Its card in flight keeps the old rules:} other {Its # cards in flight keep the old rules:}}
workflow.form.heirCards.description: Under a project inheriting a change of workflow defaults, in the dialog before saving them: its cards already started, listed below (glossary 2.1: old rules).

workflow.form.heirElsewhere.description: A project of another open workspace inheriting a change of Combwork’s workflow defaults, in the dialog before saving them: its name, its workspace’s name, then the options that change for it, as a list.

workflow.form.heirLanes.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {Its running lane keeps the old rules until it ends:} other {Its # running lanes keep the old rules until they end:}}
workflow.form.heirLanes.description: Under a project inheriting a change of workflow defaults, in the dialog before saving them, above a list of those lanes (glossary 2.1: old rules).

workflow.form.heirs.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {This project inherits the change:} other {These # projects inherit the change:}}
workflow.form.heirs.description: In the dialog before saving workflow defaults, above the projects that use them (they don’t set the changed options themselves).

workflow.form.hoursValue.description: The value of the workflow option “Wait (hours)” (Card loops) in words, as in the Inherit box and a preset preview.

workflow.form.identity.description: Under “Commits use the project’s identity”: the identity used, from git config.

workflow.form.identityValue.description: A value of “Commits use the project’s identity” in the list of what changes before saving workflow options: on, with the name and email commits use.

workflow.form.inFlight.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {This card in flight keeps the old rules. Tick it to apply the new options to it now.} other {These cards in flight keep the old rules. Tick one to apply the new options to it now.}}
workflow.form.inFlight.description: In the dialog before saving workflow options, above the cards already started (glossary 2.1: old rules). Ticking a card records an override on it.

workflow.form.inherit.description: A button beside a workflow option set for this project: stop setting it here, and use the workspace’s or Combwork’s value.

workflow.form.inheritTip.description: The tooltip of the Inherit button of a workflow option. {value} is the value it would have.

workflow.form.inheritor.defaultMessage: Project {project} inherits these options, and the change would make its options contradict each other:
workflow.form.inheritor.description: Why saving workflow defaults was refused: a project inheriting them would have contradictory options. Its reason follows on its own line. {project} is its name.

workflow.form.invalid.defaultMessage: These options can’t be used, so every rule is off in this project:
workflow.form.invalid.description: A note atop Project Settings → Workflow: the saved options contradict each other or can’t be read; the reason follows.

workflow.form.keptCard.description: HI-2674: a card in flight keeping its target branch, in the dialog before saving workflow options. {card} is its key (HI-12), {target} a branch name.

workflow.form.keptLane.defaultMessage: {named, select, yes {Lane {name} (builder {builder}), its cards still to start too: into {target}} other {Lane of builder {builder}, its cards still to start too: into {target}}}
workflow.form.keptLane.description: HI-2674: a running lane keeping its target branch, in the dialog before saving workflow options. {builder} is an agent’s name, {target} a branch name.

workflow.form.keptTargets.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {A target is set as a card or lane starts. This one keeps merging into its own, even if you tick it:} other {A target is set as a card or lane starts. These keep merging into their own, even if you tick them:}}
workflow.form.keptTargets.description: HI-2674: in the dialog before saving workflow options that change Work merges into (the target branch), above the lanes and cards in flight that keep their own target. Ticking is the cards’ checkboxes above, which apply the other options.

workflow.form.labels.description: The placeholder of the labels field of “Your OK before merging”.

workflow.form.labelsValue.description: A value of “Your OK before merging” in the list of what changes before saving workflow options. {labels} is a list of card labels.

workflow.form.lane.description: A running lane in the dialog before saving workflow options: its builder agent and its name.

workflow.form.laneUnnamed.description: A running lane without a name in the dialog before saving workflow options: its builder agent.

workflow.form.lanes.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {This running lane keeps the old rules until it ends:} other {These running lanes keep the old rules until they end:}}
workflow.form.lanes.description: In the dialog before saving workflow options, above a list of lanes (glossary 2.1: old rules).

workflow.form.levelConfirm.defaultMessage: Projects that don’t set these options themselves use the new defaults from their next card.
workflow.form.levelConfirm.description: The message of the dialog before saving workflow defaults (Settings → Workflow defaults or Settings → Workspace).

workflow.form.levelForGit.description: Beside the None · Git choice above workflow defaults, while Git is chosen.

workflow.form.levelForJj.description: Beside the None · Git · jj choice above workflow defaults, while jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799) is chosen. Keep jj.

workflow.form.levelForNone.defaultMessage: The defaults of projects without version control.
workflow.form.levelForNone.description: Beside the None · Git choice above workflow defaults, while None is chosen.

workflow.form.levelGit.description: The choice of the defaults for Git projects (glossary 2.1: keep).

workflow.form.levelJj.description: The choice of the defaults for projects using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799). Keep jj: the tool’s name, lower case.

workflow.form.levelNone.description: The choice of the defaults for projects without version control (glossary 2.1: None).

workflow.form.levelPlatform.description: Accessible name of the None · Git choice above workflow defaults: which version control’s defaults are shown (glossary 2.1).

workflow.form.loadFailed.description: An error showing Project Settings → Workflow. {error} says why.

workflow.form.loopsReadNote.defaultMessage: Read when a loop starts: a loop already running keeps its own, and one started with its own (“rounds: 5, wait: 2h”) keeps those.
workflow.form.loopsReadNote.description: Under the workflow options “Rounds” and “Wait (hours)” (Card loops), when a change applies. “rounds: 5, wait: 2h” is what the user types to an agent: keep it in English.

workflow.form.minutesValue.description: The value of the workflow option “Design check wait (minutes)” (Card loops) in words, as in the Inherit box.

workflow.form.neverOff.fileLocks.defaultMessage: File locks, while their own setting has them on.
workflow.form.neverOff.fileLocks.description: A protection that stays on with every rule off: agents can’t edit one file at once (its own setting decides).

workflow.form.neverOff.folderGit.defaultMessage: No branch switch, pull or other git that changes the folder while an agent works there.
workflow.form.neverOff.folderGit.description: A protection that stays on with every rule off.

workflow.form.neverOff.indexLock.description: A protection that stays on with every rule off. Keep index.lock (a file name).

workflow.form.neverOff.queue.defaultMessage: The merge queue moves a target branch only if nothing else moved it meanwhile.
workflow.form.neverOff.queue.description: A protection that stays on with every rule off (glossary 2.1: merge queue).

workflow.form.neverOffHead.defaultMessage: What never turns off, to keep your work safe:
workflow.form.neverOffHead.description: Above the list of protections that stay on with every rule off (SPEC §16.6.4), in the Workflow section.

workflow.form.noChanges.defaultMessage: No option changes: only the preset they started from.
workflow.form.noChanges.description: In the dialog before saving workflow options, when no option’s value changes.

workflow.form.noChecks.description: Under “Checks pass before review” when it has none.

workflow.form.noHeirs.defaultMessage: No project inherits the change now: each sets these options itself, or none uses this version control.
workflow.form.noHeirs.description: In the dialog before saving workflow defaults, when no open project uses the changed options.

workflow.form.noIdentity.defaultMessage: No name and email are set in git config yet.
workflow.form.noIdentity.description: Under “Commits use the project’s identity” when git has no identity configured.

workflow.form.noPreset.description: The Workflow section’s preset line when the options didn’t start from a preset (glossary 2.1: preset).

workflow.form.noneValue.description: An empty value in the list of what changes before saving workflow options: no checks, no commands, no folders.

workflow.form.notEnforced.defaultMessage: Workflow rules aren’t enforced (Settings → Advanced). These options are saved, and apply once the rules are enforced again.
workflow.form.notEnforced.description: A note atop Project Settings → Workflow while the switch "Workflow rules are enforced" is off.

workflow.form.openAdvanced.description: A button beside the note that workflow rules aren’t enforced: opens Settings → Advanced.

workflow.form.otherTargets.description: HI-2556: the placeholder of the field “Other branches work can merge into” (branch names besides Work merges into). Keep 1.2.0 as it is.

workflow.form.overMax.defaultMessage: This project has {count, plural, one {# agent} other {# agents}}: none is removed, but no agent can be added until it has fewer than {max, number}.
workflow.form.overMax.description: Under the workflow option “Maximum agents” (HI-2001) when the project already has more agents ({count}) than it is set to ({max}): nobody can add one (HI-2058), neither the user nor the Assistant.

workflow.form.paste.description: The button pasting workflow options copied from another project.

workflow.form.pasteApply.description: The confirm button of the dialog pasting workflow options.

workflow.form.pasteBad.defaultMessage: That isn’t workflow options copied from Combwork.
workflow.form.pasteBad.description: An error pasting workflow options: the text isn’t the JSON Combwork copies.

workflow.form.pasteMessage.defaultMessage: Paste options copied from a project with the same version control. They replace the form’s, to save afterwards.
workflow.form.pasteMessage.description: The message of the dialog pasting workflow options as JSON.

workflow.form.pastePlatform.defaultMessage: These options are for another version control.
workflow.form.pastePlatform.description: An error pasting workflow options: they were copied from a project with another version control.

workflow.form.pasteTitle.description: The title of the dialog pasting workflow options as JSON.

workflow.form.preset.description: A row of Project Settings → Workflow (glossary 2.1: preset): one choice that fills in every option.

workflow.form.presetDesc.defaultMessage: Fills in every option at once. Changing an option afterwards makes it Custom.
workflow.form.presetDesc.description: Under the row "Preset" of Project Settings → Workflow. Custom is a preset’s name: as translated there.

workflow.form.presetsLabel.description: Accessible name of the list of presets in the Workflow section (glossary 2.1: preset).

workflow.form.previewChanges.defaultMessage: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing here changes.} one {Marked: the option it changes here.} other {Marked: the # options it changes here.}}
workflow.form.previewChanges.description: In a preset’s preview in the Workflow section: how many of the options it sets differ from the form now (those are marked).

workflow.form.previewHead.description: Above the list of options a preset sets, in its preview in the Workflow section (glossary 2.1: preset). {preset} is its name.

workflow.form.previewNow.description: In a preset’s preview, beside an option it changes: its value in the form now.

workflow.form.readOnly.defaultMessage: {agents} can’t be given review copies by their coding agent, so they review the builder’s folder read-only.
workflow.form.readOnly.description: Under “Reviewers” (G17) when some reviewing agents use a coding agent that Combwork can’t give review copies (folders at the exact revision, glossary 2.5: review copy). {agents} is a list of agent names.

workflow.form.removeCheck.description: The tooltip of the button removing a check from “Checks pass before review”.

workflow.form.retargetCard.description: HI-2680: a card the retarget moves to the new Work merges into, in the dialog before saving. {card} is its key (HI-12).

workflow.form.retargetChoice.defaultMessage: Also retarget what can move from {from} to {to}: {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} and {slots, plural, one {# free slot} other {# free slots}}
workflow.form.retargetChoice.description: HI-2680: a tick box in the dialog before saving workflow options that change Work merges into: after saving, move the Todo cards with no work of their own and the free slots still on the old branch {from} to the new one {to}. Card and slot counts.

workflow.form.retargetDone.defaultMessage: {skipped, plural, =0 {Moved to {to}: {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} and {slots, plural, one {# slot} other {# slots}}} other {Moved to {to}: {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} and {slots, plural, one {# slot} other {# slots}}; # left where they were}}
workflow.form.retargetDone.description: HI-2680: a notification after the retarget: how many cards and slots moved to the new branch {to}, and how many were left (each listed with why in its text).

workflow.form.retargetFailed.defaultMessage: The options were saved, but nothing was retargeted
workflow.form.retargetFailed.description: HI-2680: an error’s title: the workflow options were saved, but the retarget that should follow failed. Its text says why.

workflow.form.retargetKeep.defaultMessage: {what}: {why, select, work {it has work on its branch} started {already started} lane {a running lane keeps its branch until it ends} queued {it is in the merge queue} notInTarget {it has commits {to} doesn’t have} reviewed {its reviewed work would bring other commits} noLine {it works in the project folder} lent {lent} dirty {it has changes not committed} busy {in use} unmerged {it holds commits {from} lacks} targetChanged {the target changed meanwhile} refused {not allowed now} changed {it changed meanwhile} moved {it moved meanwhile} gone {its folder is gone} setAside {set aside: look at its folder} other {Combwork can’t tell}}
workflow.form.retargetKeep.description: HI-2680, HI-2753: a card, slot or lane the retarget leaves where it is, and why (a select: keep the keys). {what} is its name; {from} the old branch, {to} the new one. queued: in the merge queue; notInTarget: a started card with commits the new branch lacks; reviewed: a reviewed card whose change would differ on the new branch; noLine: it has no branch of its own.

workflow.form.retargetLane.defaultMessage: {hasCard, select, yes {{lane}, with its card {card} {title}: to the new branch} other {{lane}: its next cards start from the new branch}}
workflow.form.retargetLane.description: HI-2753: a running lane (a card loop) that the retarget moves to the new Work merges into, in the dialog before saving: with its card in flight ({card}, its key, and {title}), both in one step, or with none in flight. {lane} names the lane (its name and builder). Keep the select keys.

workflow.form.retargetSkipped.defaultMessage: {what}: {why, select, targetChanged {the target changed meanwhile} refused {not allowed now} changed {it changed meanwhile} busy {in use} dirty {it has changes not committed} moved {it moved meanwhile} unmerged {it holds commits the old branch lacks} gone {its folder is gone} setAside {set aside until you remove it: look at its folder first} failed {it couldn’t be moved; Combwork looks at it again} other {Combwork can’t tell}}
workflow.form.retargetSkipped.description: HI-2680: a line of the notification after the retarget: a card or slot left where it was ({what}: its key or name), and why (a select: keep the keys).

workflow.form.retargetSlot.description: HI-2680: a free slot the retarget moves to the new Work merges into (its folder detached at the new branch), in the dialog before saving. {slot} is its name (slot-a).

workflow.form.retargetStarted.defaultMessage: {card} {title}: to the new branch, its branch and work kept
workflow.form.retargetStarted.description: HI-2753: a card already started (in Doing, Review or Passed) that the retarget moves to the new Work merges into, in the dialog before saving: its own branch and commits stay, since all of its work is its own. {card} is its key (HI-12).

workflow.form.retargetStays.description: HI-2680: in the dialog before saving workflow options, above what the retarget leaves on the old branch {from}, each with why.

workflow.form.save.description: The button saving the workflow options (it shows what changes first).

workflow.form.saveBlocked.defaultMessage: Resolve what the options say first.
workflow.form.saveBlocked.description: The tooltip of Save… in the Workflow section while some options contradict each other (their reasons are shown under them).

workflow.form.saved.description: A notification: the workflow options were saved.

workflow.form.stageName.description: Accessible name of a stage’s name box under “Stage names” (glossary 2.2: stage). {stage} is its default name.

workflow.form.stageNamesValue.defaultMessage: {n, plural, =0 {The default names} one {# stage renamed} other {# stages renamed}}
workflow.form.stageNamesValue.description: A value of “Stage names” in the list of what changes before saving workflow options, and in a preset’s preview (glossary 2.2: stage).

workflow.form.startedFrom.description: Project Settings → Workflow: the options were changed after a preset was chosen. {preset} is its name.

workflow.form.stepWaitNote.defaultMessage: A design left unchecked longer shows its card as stalled; one already posted keeps its wait.
workflow.form.stepWaitNote.description: Under the workflow option “Design check wait (minutes)” (Card loops), when a change applies.

workflow.form.templateIdentityOff.defaultMessage: The template turns the project identity on, but this project’s git config has no name and email, so it stays off.
workflow.form.templateIdentityOff.description: A note atop the Workflow section (HI-1910), with a template's options filled in: it turns the project identity (G12) on, but the project's git config has none. Glossary: identity.

workflow.form.templateNoCommand.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {This project has no command for the check {checks} yet: add it under Checks before cards need it.} other {This project has no commands for the checks {checks} yet: add them under Checks before cards need them.}}
workflow.form.templateNoCommand.description: A note atop the Workflow section (HI-1910), with the template's options filled in: checks ({checks}, a list of names; {count} of them) have no command in this project. Checks is the group below: as translated there. Glossary: check.

workflow.form.templateOtherPlatform.defaultMessage: The workflow of {template} is for {platform}, and {project} doesn’t use it now, so it wasn’t filled in.
workflow.form.templateOtherPlatform.description: A notification (HI-1910): a loaded template's workflow ({template}) is for a version control ({platform}: None or Git) the project ({project}) no longer uses (switched meanwhile).

workflow.form.use.description: A button in a preset’s preview: fills the form with it (saved only with Save…). {preset} is its name.

workflow.group.checks.description: A heading of the Workflow section: the options about the checks that must pass (glossary 2.3: checks).

workflow.group.loops.description: A heading of the Workflow section: how card loops run, a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn (glossary: card loop).

workflow.group.merging.description: A heading of the Workflow section (Git): the options about how and where work is merged.

workflow.group.review.description: A heading of the Version Control tab’s Workflow section: the options about reviewing a card’s work.

workflow.group.stages.description: A heading of the Workflow section: the names of the board’s stages (glossary 2.2: stage).

workflow.group.team.description: A heading of the Workflow section: how many agents the project has (its team, HI-2001).

workflow.group.where.description: A heading of the Workflow section (Git): the options about the folders cards are built in and the commits made there (glossary 2.6, G11).

workflow.group.work.description: A heading of the Workflow section for a project without version control: what a card’s work is, and when cards start.

workflow.mergeChoice.answer.description: The user's answer to the merge queue's question before an upgraded project's first merge, kept on the card as the user's own comment: the two workflow options they chose, each its name ({styleTitle}: Merge style; {messageTitle}: Commit message) and the value chosen ({style}: Squash, say; {message}: a value of Commit message). The names and values are the workflow options' own texts, already translated: arrange them as your language writes such a list.

workflow.missing.create.description: HI-2807: the button beside a missing branch: creates it from the branch picked, without switching to it.

workflow.missing.from.description: HI-2807: the accessible name of the drop-down of branches a missing branch {branch} can be created from.

workflow.missing.line.description: HI-2807: under Work merges into or Other branches work can merge into, for a branch named there that the repository hasn’t got; a drop-down of branches and a Create button follow.

workflow.missing.save.defaultMessage: Create {branches} first: {n, plural, one {it doesn’t} other {they don’t}} exist yet.
workflow.missing.save.description: HI-2807: why Save is disabled in the Workflow section: branches named as targets ({branches}, {n} of them) don’t exist.

workflow.move.answer.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user's answer to a For you request (Approve, Decline, a reply).

workflow.move.declarePaths.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: saying which files are its work (a project without version control).

workflow.move.loopStep.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move (#1382): a step between a card loop's builder and reviewer that moves nothing (a design posted for a check, its answer).

workflow.move.move.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: dragging it to another column.

workflow.move.putBack.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: putting a started card back in Todo.

workflow.move.removeFromQueue.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user taking it out of the merge queue.

workflow.move.reportMerge.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the agent saying it merged the work.

workflow.move.resolveOnBuilder.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move (HI-2959): the user's Resolve on a builder on a forward merge the merge queue returned (Combwork's card bringing one branch up to date with another): it ends, and a new card is made for a builder to resolve its conflict.

workflow.move.retryMerge.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user's Retry merge on the merge queue's card.

workflow.move.start.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move ("… isn't possible from there"): starting work on it.

workflow.move.startReview.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: a reviewer beginning a review.

workflow.move.submit.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: sending its work to Review.

workflow.move.verdict.description: A move on a card, named in a refused move: a reviewer passing or failing it (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.nextVersion.button.description: HI-2807: a button under Work merges into, while it is a version branch (1.3.0): opens the Start the next version dialog.

workflow.nextVersion.done.defaultMessage: Started {name} from {from}: work merges into {name} now{added, select, yes {, and {from} is one of the other branches work can merge into} other {}}.
workflow.nextVersion.done.description: HI-2807: a notification after Start the next version. {name} the new branch, {from} the release.

workflow.nextVersion.doneMoved.defaultMessage: Started {name} from {from}: work merges into {name} now. Moved {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} and {slots, plural, one {# slot} other {# slots}} to it{skipped, plural, =0 {} other {; # left where they were}}.
workflow.nextVersion.doneMoved.description: HI-2807: a notification after Start the next version with Also retarget ticked.

workflow.nextVersion.enterName.description: HI-2807: an error in the Start the next version dialog: the name box is empty.

workflow.nextVersion.message.defaultMessage: Work merges into {from} now. The next version gets a branch of its own, made from {from} as it is:
workflow.nextVersion.message.description: HI-2807: the Start the next version dialog’s first line. {from} is the release branch.

workflow.nextVersion.name.description: HI-2807: the label of the box with the new branch’s name in the Start the next version dialog.

workflow.nextVersion.noStart.defaultMessage: {from} isn’t a branch in this repository, so nothing can start from it.
workflow.nextVersion.noStart.description: HI-2807: the Start the next version dialog when the release branch doesn’t exist.

workflow.nextVersion.planFailed.defaultMessage: Couldn’t read what Start the next version would do

workflow.nextVersion.start.description: HI-2807: the Start the next version dialog’s button.

workflow.nextVersion.starting.description: HI-2807: the Start the next version dialog’s button while it runs.

workflow.nextVersion.stays.defaultMessage: Running lanes and started cards stay on {from}.
workflow.nextVersion.stays.description: HI-2807: under the steps in the Start the next version dialog: what doesn’t move.

workflow.nextVersion.stepAdd.defaultMessage: Add {from} to Other branches work can merge into
workflow.nextVersion.stepAdd.description: HI-2807: a step the Start the next version dialog lists. Other branches work can merge into is an option’s name: as translated there.

workflow.nextVersion.stepCreate.description: HI-2807: a step the Start the next version dialog lists: make the branch {name} at {from}’s head, the commit {commit} (short hash).

workflow.nextVersion.stepListed.defaultMessage: {from} stays in Other branches work can merge into
workflow.nextVersion.stepListed.description: HI-2807: a step the Start the next version dialog lists, when the release branch is listed there already.

workflow.nextVersion.stepTarget.description: HI-2807: a step the Start the next version dialog lists: the option Work merges into (as translated there) moves from {from} to {name}.

workflow.nextVersion.tip.defaultMessage: A new branch from {from} for the next version: work merges into it from then on, and {from} stays a branch work can merge into.
workflow.nextVersion.tip.description: HI-2807: tooltip of Start the next version…. {from} is the release branch (Work merges into now).

workflow.nextVersion.title.description: HI-2807: the title of the Start the next version dialog.

workflow.option.commands.desc.defaultMessage: The command each named check runs. A run counts as the check only when it runs that command.
workflow.option.commands.desc.description: What the workflow setting “Check commands” does.

workflow.option.commands.title.description: A workflow setting: the command each named check runs (the checks of “Checks pass before review”).

workflow.option.commitMessage.desc.defaultMessage: The message of the commit the merge queue makes: Combwork’s names the card’s key and title and adds Combwork’s trailers, and the branch’s own uses the message its commits have, with no card key or trailers, while Combwork still knows which card it merged.
workflow.option.commitMessage.desc.description: What the workflow option “Commit message” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue). Trailers are git’s name for the “Key: value” lines at the end of a commit message: keep the word if your language’s git terms do.

workflow.option.commitMessage.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G19): the message of the commit Combwork’s merge queue makes when it merges a card (a merge commit, or a squash’s one commit).

workflow.option.dependenciesDone.desc.defaultMessage: A card that waits for others can’t start before their work is in.
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.desc.description: What the workflow option “Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged” does.

workflow.option.dependenciesDone.none.defaultMessage: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.none.description: A workflow option for a project without version control (glossary 2.6, N6).

workflow.option.dependenciesDone.title.defaultMessage: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged

workflow.option.excluded.desc.defaultMessage: The whole project folder, apart from these folders and files (.combwork always).
workflow.option.excluded.desc.description: What the workflow option “What the work is” does: the folders and files listed are left out of a card’s work.

workflow.option.excluded.title.description: A workflow option for a project without version control (glossary 2.6, N4).

workflow.option.fileLocks.desc.defaultMessage: What happens when an agent tries to edit a file another agent in the same folder is editing.
workflow.option.fileLocks.desc.description: What the workflow option “File locks” does.

workflow.option.fileLocks.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, N7): what happens when two agents in the same folder edit the same file.

workflow.option.finish.desc.defaultMessage: When a card is done: once Combwork’s merge queue has merged it, once its agent has merged it and Combwork finds the work in the target branch, once it is committed, or whenever it is moved there.
workflow.option.finish.desc.description: What the workflow option “Who merges” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue).

workflow.option.focusedTests.desc.defaultMessage: When a card is submitted, the project’s command chooses the tests its change needs (or its builder names them, for its reviewer to check), and the merge queue runs them on the merged result, moving the target only once they pass.
workflow.option.focusedTests.desc.description: What the workflow option “Each card’s focused tests pass on the merged result” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue).

workflow.option.focusedTests.title.defaultMessage: Each card’s focused tests pass on the merged result
workflow.option.focusedTests.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G20): the tests a card’s change needs are chosen when it is submitted, and Combwork’s merge queue runs them on its work merged with the target branch.

workflow.option.folder.desc.defaultMessage: In its own folder, a slot Combwork lends to the card or its lane, each card is built on a branch of its own, apart from other agents’ work; in the project folder, everyone sees each other’s unfinished changes.
workflow.option.folder.desc.description: What the workflow option “Where cards are built” does (glossary 2.5: slot, a worktree Combwork lends to a card or a lane).

workflow.option.followRemote.desc.defaultMessage: Before each test merge, the merge queue fetches the remote branch the target tracks and tests on its latest commit, pushes each merge there only if nobody pushed meanwhile (testing again if they did), and then brings the local target up to date.
workflow.option.followRemote.desc.description: What the workflow option “The target branch follows its remote” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue; 2.5: test merge). “Push the target branch after merging” is another option’s name.

workflow.option.followRemote.title.defaultMessage: The target branch follows its remote
workflow.option.followRemote.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G21): the target branch is the one it tracks on its remote; Combwork’s merge queue fetches it before each test merge and publishes each merge there first.

workflow.option.identity.desc.defaultMessage: Commits are made with the name and email from the project’s git config (else your global one).
workflow.option.identity.desc.description: What the workflow option “Commits use the project’s identity” does.

workflow.option.loopRounds.desc.defaultMessage: How many rounds a card gets in a card loop (a build and its review each) before its agents stop and ask you, when the loop doesn’t say.
workflow.option.loopRounds.desc.description: What the workflow option “Rounds” does (Card loops).

workflow.option.loopRounds.title.description: A workflow option, under Card loops: how many rounds (a build and its review) a card gets before its agents ask you.

workflow.option.loopStepWaitMinutes.desc.defaultMessage: How many minutes, up to 4 hours, a card loop’s builder waits for its reviewer to check a design it posted before it goes ahead as posted.
workflow.option.loopStepWaitMinutes.desc.description: What the workflow option “Design check wait (minutes)” does (Card loops). A design: the plan a builder posts on its card before building.

workflow.option.loopStepWaitMinutes.titl.description: A workflow option, under Card loops: how long a builder waits for its reviewer to check a design it posted.

workflow.option.loopWaitHours.desc.defaultMessage: How many hours, up to a day, an agent in a card loop waits with no change before it tells you, when the loop doesn’t say.
workflow.option.loopWaitHours.desc.description: What the workflow option “Wait (hours)” does (Card loops).

workflow.option.loopWaitHours.title.description: A workflow option, under Card loops: how many hours an agent in a card loop waits with no change before it tells you.

workflow.option.loopWakes.desc.defaultMessage: When a card with a reviewer arrives in Review, Combwork wakes the reviewer, and on the review’s verdict the card’s builder; off, only the agents’ own card watches wake them.
workflow.option.loopWakes.desc.description: What the workflow option “Wake reviewers and builders” does.

workflow.option.loopWakes.title.description: A workflow option, under Card loops: Combwork wakes the agents of a card loop for its handoffs (glossary: card loop).

workflow.option.maxAgents.desc.defaultMessage: Your team size: the most agents this project has, whoever adds them (you, the Assistant or a program using the Agent API), and lowering it removes none.
workflow.option.maxAgents.desc.description: What the workflow option “Maximum agents” does (HI-2058: it binds the user too). Agent API is the name of a Combwork feature.

workflow.option.maxAgents.title.description: A workflow option (HI-2001): the most agents the project has, its team size. Nobody adds agents past it: the user, the Combwork Assistant or a program (HI-2058).

workflow.option.mergeChecks.desc.defaultMessage: Combwork’s merge queue runs these named commands on the card’s work merged with the target branch, and moves the target only once each one has passed.
workflow.option.mergeChecks.desc.description: What the workflow option “Checks pass on the merged result” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue).

workflow.option.mergeChecks.jjDesc.defaultMessage: Combwork runs these named commands on the candidate, in a check copy of its own, and offers the candidate for you to integrate only once each one has passed. One that fails sends the card back to its builder.
workflow.option.mergeChecks.jjDesc.description: What the workflow option “Checks pass on the candidate” does, for a project using jj (HI-2938). A check copy is a working folder Combwork keeps for checks (glossary).

workflow.option.mergeChecks.jjTitle.description: The workflow option “Checks pass on the merged result” (G9) for a project using jj (HI-2938): named commands Combwork runs on the candidate it builds for the user to integrate. Candidate: the commit Combwork builds.

workflow.option.mergeChecks.title.defaultMessage: Checks pass on the merged result
workflow.option.mergeChecks.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G9): named commands Combwork’s merge queue runs on a card’s work merged with the target branch.

workflow.option.mergeInstall.desc.defaultMessage: Before the checks on the merged result, the merge queue installs the dependencies afresh, and always does when the lock file or manifests changed.
workflow.option.mergeInstall.desc.description: What the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch” does. Lock file: as in the glossary (G15 value).

workflow.option.mergeInstall.jjDesc.defaultMessage: Before the checks on a candidate, its check copy installs the dependencies afresh: always, or when the lock file or manifests changed.
workflow.option.mergeInstall.jjDesc.description: What the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch” does, for a project using jj (HI-2938). A check copy is a working folder Combwork keeps for checks. Lock file: as in the glossary.

workflow.option.mergeInstall.jjTitle.description: The workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch” for a project using jj (HI-2938): before the checks on the candidate.

workflow.option.mergeInstall.title.description: A workflow option (G9’s install): when the merge queue installs the project’s dependencies afresh before the merge checks.

workflow.option.noSelfReview.desc.defaultMessage: Always on while a reviewer agent checks the work.
workflow.option.noSelfReview.desc.description: What the workflow option “Nobody reviews their own work” does.

workflow.option.noSelfReview.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G2 and N2).

workflow.option.okBefore.desc.defaultMessage: A card waits for your OK before it is merged: never, only cards with these labels, or every card.
workflow.option.okBefore.desc.description: What the workflow option “Your OK before merging” does.

workflow.option.otherTargets.desc.defaultMessage: Branches a lane or a card can merge into instead (its Merges into), each through its own merge queue with the same merge checks, separated by commas.
workflow.option.otherTargets.desc.description: What the workflow option “Other branches work can merge into” does (HI-2556). Merges into is the lane’s and card’s field: as translated there.

workflow.option.otherTargets.title.defaultMessage: Other branches work can merge into
workflow.option.otherTargets.title.description: A workflow option (HI-2556, G7b): branches besides “Work merges into” that a lane or a card can be set to merge into (its “Merges into”). Darren’s name for it.

workflow.option.preChecks.desc.defaultMessage: A card goes to review only once each of these named commands has passed on its work.
workflow.option.preChecks.desc.description: What the workflow option “Checks pass before review” does.

workflow.option.preChecks.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G3 and N3): named commands that must pass before a card goes to review.

workflow.option.pushTarget.desc.defaultMessage: After each merge, the merge queue pushes the target branch to the remote it tracks (or the only remote, or origin), never forced, and pauses, saying why, when the push is refused or fails.
workflow.option.pushTarget.desc.description: What the workflow option “Push the target branch after merging” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue). Origin is git’s usual name for a remote: keep it.

workflow.option.pushTarget.title.defaultMessage: Push the target branch after merging
workflow.option.pushTarget.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G18): after Combwork’s merge queue merges a card, it pushes the target branch to its remote.

workflow.option.review.desc.defaultMessage: A card goes to Review when its builder submits it and moves on only once it passes, waiting for your OK after the reviewer when you check too.
workflow.option.review.desc.description: What the workflow option “Work is reviewed before it’s merged” does.

workflow.option.review.none.defaultMessage: Who checks the work before it’s done
workflow.option.review.none.description: A workflow option for a project without version control (glossary 2.6, N1).

workflow.option.review.shared.defaultMessage: Work is reviewed before it’s done
workflow.option.review.shared.description: The workflow option G1 when everyone works in the project folder, where the work is on the target meanwhile (glossary 2.6, G1 shared folder).

workflow.option.review.title.defaultMessage: Work is reviewed before it’s merged
workflow.option.review.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G1): who reviews a card’s work before it is merged.

workflow.option.reviewerMode.desc.defaultMessage: One reviewer per lane, or a shared pool: Combwork gives each card submitted in a pool lane, oldest first, to the next free reviewer that didn’t build it.
workflow.option.reviewerMode.desc.description: What the workflow option “Reviewers” does (glossary 2.6, G17; glossary: lane, pool).

workflow.option.reviewerMode.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G17): whether each lane has its own reviewer agent or the lanes share a pool of reviewers.

workflow.option.reviewers.desc.defaultMessage: With two, both must pass the same change.
workflow.option.reviewers.desc.description: What the workflow option “Reviewers per card” does.

workflow.option.reviewers.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G1b): how many reviewer agents must pass a card.

workflow.option.sameness.desc.defaultMessage: With Same change, a pass carries over to a clean rebase or squash of the same change; with Exact revision only, any new revision makes it stale.
workflow.option.sameness.desc.description: What the workflow option “A pass survives a clean rebase” does.

workflow.option.sameness.title.defaultMessage: A pass survives a clean rebase

workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.desc.defaultMessage: A submit warns, never refuses, when its commit takes in files another agent is editing in the project folder.
workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.desc.description: What the workflow option “Warn when a commit includes another agent’s files” does.

workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.titl.defaultMessage: Warn when a commit includes another agent’s files

workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.desc.defaultMessage: Before a card starts in a slot, the slot is brought to the latest work of the target branch, and its dependencies are installed again when the lock file changed.
workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.desc.description: What the workflow option “Slots are brought up to date before each card” does (glossary 2.5: slot; lock file, as in the G15 value).

workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.title.defaultMessage: Slots are brought up to date before each card
workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G15; glossary 2.5: slot): before a card starts in a slot, the slot is brought to the target branch’s latest work.

workflow.option.stageNames.desc.defaultMessage: Rename any stage the board shows: a name changes no rule and applies at once.
workflow.option.stageNames.desc.description: What the workflow option “Stage names” does (glossary 2.2: stage).

workflow.option.stageNames.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, N5; glossary 2.2: stage): your own names for the board’s stages.

workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.desc.defaultMessage: A card goes to review only once its builder’s own runs and background commands have stopped.
workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.desc.description: What the workflow option “Agents stop what they started before review” does.

workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.title.defaultMessage: Agents stop what they started before review

workflow.option.strict.desc.defaultMessage: When the target branch has moved on since the review, the merge queue brings the work up to date in its own folder first, and returns the card if that conflicts or makes a different change.
workflow.option.strict.desc.description: What the workflow option “Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue; Squash is the merge style’s value).

workflow.option.strict.jjDesc.defaultMessage: When the target bookmark has moved on since the review, Combwork first brings the work up to date with it (merged in, or rebased with Squash), then builds the candidate on that, and returns the card if that conflicts or makes a different change. Rebase builds its candidate on the bookmark anyway.
workflow.option.strict.jjDesc.description: What the workflow option “The candidate brings work up to date first” does, for a project using jj (HI-2871). A bookmark is jj’s name for a branch; Squash and Rebase are the candidate style’s values.

workflow.option.strict.jjTitle.defaultMessage: The candidate brings work up to date first
workflow.option.strict.jjTitle.description: The workflow option “Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges” (G8, strict) for a project using jj (HI-2871): before building the candidate the user integrates, Combwork brings the card’s work up to date with the target bookmark.

workflow.option.strict.title.defaultMessage: Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges
workflow.option.strict.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G8, strict): a card’s work must contain the target branch’s latest commit before it is merged; Combwork’s merge queue brings it up to date itself.

workflow.option.style.desc.defaultMessage: How a card’s work is merged into the target branch.
workflow.option.style.desc.description: What the workflow option “Merge style” does.

workflow.option.style.jjDesc.defaultMessage: Once a card passes, Combwork builds a candidate from it on the target bookmark: a merge commit, one squashed commit, or its commits copied on top. You move the bookmark to the candidate yourself; Combwork never does.
workflow.option.style.jjDesc.description: What the workflow option “Candidate style” does, for a project using jj (HI-2871). A bookmark is jj’s name for a branch: keep it as jj’s term.

workflow.option.style.jjTitle.description: The workflow option “Merge style” (G6) for a project using jj (HI-2871): how the candidate commit Combwork builds for the user to integrate is made (merge commit, squash or rebase). Candidate: the commit Combwork builds.

workflow.option.target.desc.defaultMessage: The branch a card’s work is merged into: the repository’s default branch when left empty.
workflow.option.target.desc.description: What the workflow option “Work merges into” does.

workflow.option.target.title.description: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G7): the target branch.

workflow.preset.custom.description: The workflow preset shown when the options no longer match a preset (glossary 2.1).

workflow.preset.note.teamFocused.defaultMessage: Team runs each card’s focused tests on the merged result when the project has a command that runs them: set it under Each card’s focused tests.
workflow.preset.note.teamFocused.description: Under the preset choice of Project Settings → Workflow while Team is chosen (glossary 2.1: Team; G20: Each card’s focused tests is an option’s name, as translated there).

workflow.preset.pair.description: A workflow preset (glossary 2.1): a builder and a reviewer.

workflow.preset.pairAgent.description: A workflow preset (glossary 2.1, Pair): a builder and a reviewer, and the builder merges each card itself.

workflow.preset.solo.description: A workflow preset (glossary 2.1): one person, one agent at a time, no reviewer.

workflow.preset.team.description: A workflow preset (glossary 2.1): several builders and reviewers, stricter checks.

workflow.presetsNotice.choose.description: A button of the one-time presets notice: opens the first project’s Version Control tab at Workflow.

workflow.presetsNotice.notNow.description: A button of the one-time presets notice: dismisses it for good.

workflow.presetsNotice.text.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {{projects} works} other {{projects} work}} as before this version. A preset sets up a workflow in one click: who reviews the work, which checks pass first and who merges.
workflow.presetsNotice.text.description: The one-time notice after the upgrade to 1.0 (glossary 2.1: preset, workflow). {projects} is a list of project names; {n} how many.

workflow.refused.approval.given.change.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Your OK before merging.
workflow.refused.approval.given.change.description: Where the rule that waits for the user's OK is changed.

workflow.refused.approval.given.message.defaultMessage: {card} waits for the OK before merging.
workflow.refused.approval.given.message.description: A refused move: the user has to approve the card first (glossary 2.3: approval; Version Control → Your OK before merging).

workflow.refused.approval.given.next.defaultMessage: Wait for the OK, given on the card or in For you.
workflow.refused.approval.given.next.description: The next step after a move refused for want of the user’s approval.

workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.messag.defaultMessage: A plain number is not a card reference.
workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.messag.description: A refused intent: the card was named by a bare number.

workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.next.defaultMessage: Name the card by its key: {key}.
workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.next.description: How to name a card instead of a bare number: by its key, {key} (such as AM-12).

workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..defaultMessage: {why, select, ambiguous {{revision} is the start of more than one commit here: give more of it. {head} is checked out.} other {{revision} isn't what's checked out here: {head} is.}}
workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..description: A refused check run or submission (HI-2671): the revision named ({revision}, as given, a commit id or its start) is not the checked-out commit ({head}, its first 12 characters). why=ambiguous: {revision} is the start of the checked-out commit but also of another one, so more of its characters are needed.

workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..defaultMessage: Run the check where {revision} is checked out, or without a revision.
workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..description: The next step after a check run named the wrong revision.

workflow.refused.done.contained.change.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Who merges.
workflow.refused.done.contained.change.description: Where the rule that checks a merge is changed.

workflow.refused.done.contained.message.description: A refused Done: the approved revision is not in the target branch. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.done.contained.next.defaultMessage: Merge {revision} into {target}, then report the merge again.
workflow.refused.done.contained.next.description: The next step after a refused report of a merge.

workflow.refused.evidence.changed.messag.defaultMessage: What Combwork read for {card} changed while it decided.
workflow.refused.evidence.changed.messag.description: A refused intent: a branch head, a file or another card the rule depends on changed between Combwork's reading it and recording the move. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.evidence.changed.next.defaultMessage: Try again: Combwork reads it afresh.
workflow.refused.evidence.changed.next.description: The next step after a refusal because what a rule read changed meanwhile.

workflow.refused.forward.notAgents.messa.defaultMessage: {card} brings one branch up to date with another: only the user or the Assistant acts on it.
workflow.refused.forward.notAgents.messa.description: HI-2679: a refused intent: an agent acted on a forward-merge card (Combwork’s own card that merges one of the project’s target branches into another). {card} is its key (HI-12).

workflow.refused.forward.notAgents.next.defaultMessage: Leave it to the user or the Assistant.
workflow.refused.forward.notAgents.next.description: HI-2679: the next step after an agent was refused acting on a forward-merge card.

workflow.refused.forward.resolutionTarge.defaultMessage: {card} resolves the merge of {from} into {to}, but it would start from {target} and merge there.
workflow.refused.forward.resolutionTarge.description: HI-2985: a refused start of a card made by Resolve on a builder (it merges branch {from} into branch {to} by hand): its Merges into is another branch now ({target}), as when the project’s Work merges into moved on after it was made. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.forward.resolutionTarge.defaultMessage: The user or the Assistant can set its Merges into to {to}, then start it again.
workflow.refused.forward.resolutionTarge.description: HI-2985: the next step after a refused start of a Resolve on a builder card: set its Merges into (a name in the window: as translated there) to branch {to}.

workflow.refused.integrate.approved.mess.description: A refused merge: the revision lacks the passes or approvals its rules need. {why} is a whole sentence saying what's missing.

workflow.refused.integrate.approved.next.description: The next step after a merge refused for want of approval.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Checks pass on the merged result.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..description: Where the merge checks are changed.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..defaultMessage: The merge checks failed on {card}'s merged result.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..description: A merge returned: the merge checks failed on the test merge.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..defaultMessage: Fix the failures, commit and submit the new revision.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..description: The next step after failed merge checks.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.chan.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Work is up to date before it merges.
workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.chan.description: Where the strict rule is changed.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.mess.description: A refused merge (strict): the revision is behind its target. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.next.defaultMessage: The merge queue brings it up to date itself.
workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.next.description: What happens next after the strict up-to-date rule refuses.

workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.change.defaultMessage: Settings → Advanced → Bring an agent's branch up to date after a squash merge says whether Combwork moves it or asks first.
workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.change.description: Where it is decided whether Combwork moves the branch itself or asks the user first (a setting name: use it as Combwork shows it).

workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.message.defaultMessage: {card} can't start yet: {line} still has {earlier}'s work, which was squashed into {target}.
workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.message.description: A refused start (§16.19.2): the builder's branch (in its own worktree) still has the previous card's commits, which were merged into the target as one squashed commit, so the next card's change would include them. {card} and {earlier} are card keys like AM-12; {line} a branch name; {target} the branch merged into.

workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.next.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {Leave it as it is: Combwork brings {line} up to date with {target} once the agent is idle, or asks you first, and tells the agent when {card} can start.} other {Leave it as it is: Combwork brings {line} up to date with {target} once you are idle, or asks the user, and tells you when {card} can start.}}
workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.next.description: The next step after a start refused because the branch still has squashed work: wait (end the turn); Combwork moves the branch, or asks the user first, and says when the card can start. {line} a branch name, {target} the branch merged into, {card} a card key. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.change.defaultMessage: A lane always takes one card at a time; turning off Settings → Advanced → Workflow rules are enforced turns every rule off.
workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.change.description: Where the rule that a lane takes one card at a time is changed: it has no option of its own; the switch that turns every workflow rule off (a setting name: use it as Combwork shows it).

workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.message.defaultMessage: {card} can't start yet: {earlier}, before it in its lane, isn't Done.
workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.message.description: A refused start (glossary 2.4): a lane takes one card at a time, so a card starts only once the cards before it in its lane are Done. {card} and {earlier} are card keys like AM-12.

workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.next.defaultMessage: Finish {earlier} first: once it is Done, the lane goes on to {card}.
workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.next.description: The next step after a start refused because an earlier card of the lane is not Done. {card} and {earlier} are card keys like AM-12.

workflow.refused.loop.followUpChecked.me.defaultMessage: {card}: a follow-up waits for its reviewer's check, with no going ahead without it.
workflow.refused.loop.followUpChecked.me.description: A refused going ahead unchecked (#1467): what waits is a follow-up (a change asked of reviewed work, such as a screenshot's), which only its reviewer's answer settles. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.loop.followUpChecked.ne.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {The agent waits for the reviewer's ok or gaps; if none comes, it asks you.} other {Wait for the reviewer's ok or gaps; if none comes, ask the user.}}
workflow.refused.loop.followUpChecked.ne.description: The next step after going ahead with a follow-up unchecked (#1467). ok and gaps are the reviewer's answers, as agents name them: keep them as they are. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.loop.followUpMerging.me.defaultMessage: {card} is being merged now: a follow-up can no longer take it out of the merge queue.
workflow.refused.loop.followUpMerging.me.description: A refused follow-up (#1623): a follow-up on a queued card takes it out of the merge queue first, but the queue has already begun merging this one. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.loop.followUpMerging.ne.defaultMessage: Wait for the merge; if the follow-up is still needed, put it on a new card.
workflow.refused.loop.followUpMerging.ne.description: The next step after a follow-up refused because the card is being merged now (#1623).

workflow.refused.loop.noReviewer.message.defaultMessage: {card} has no reviewer to check it: it is in no lane with a reviewer, and nobody has reviewed it yet.
workflow.refused.loop.noReviewer.message.description: A refused design or follow-up posted for a check (#1382, #1467): nobody can be woken to check it. {card} is a card key. A lane: a card loop's record of its builder and reviewer.

workflow.refused.loop.noReviewer.next.defaultMessage: Start a lane for the card with a reviewer, or say it in a comment instead.
workflow.refused.loop.noReviewer.next.description: The next step after a design or follow-up refused for want of a reviewer (#1382, #1467).

workflow.refused.loop.noStep.message.defaultMessage: {card} has no design or follow-up waiting for its check.
