workflow.refused.loop.noStep.message.description: A refused card loop step (#1382, #1467): an answer (OK, gaps) or going ahead when no design or follow-up posted by its builder waits for its reviewer's check. A follow-up: a change asked of reviewed work, such as a screenshot's. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.loop.noStep.next.defaultMessage: Read the card: it may have been answered, or the card moved on. Feedback still worth giving goes on the card as a comment.
workflow.refused.loop.noStep.next.description: The next step after a card loop step with nothing to answer (#1382): what was posted for the check may have been answered, or the card left the column it was posted in (HI-3011: a design closes when its card is put back). A reviewer with feedback for it comments on the card instead.

workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.message.defaultMessage: {card} reached its round limit: it goes on once its round-limit question is answered.
workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.message.description: A refused submission or move: the card failed as many reviews as its card loop allows (Settings → Card loops), and Combwork asked how to go on (For you); until that question is answered, its loop is paused. Read by agents and shown in the window alike: it names no one (never "the user"). {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.next.defaultMessage: The question is on the card (For you): once it is answered, Combwork wakes the agents waiting on it.
workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.next.description: The next step while a card waits at its round limit for its question (For you, a label: use it as Combwork shows it) to be answered. Read by agents and shown in the window alike: it names no one (never "the user"); Combwork then wakes the agents that wait on the card.

workflow.refused.loop.staleStep.message.defaultMessage: {card}: that is about {design}, but the one waiting for its check now is {waiting}.
workflow.refused.loop.staleStep.message.description: A refused answer to a design or follow-up, or going ahead with a design (#1382, #1467): it names an earlier one than the one waiting now, so it can't settle it. {card} is a card key; {design} and {waiting} are their ids, such as AM-12/s40.

workflow.refused.loop.staleStep.next.defaultMessage: Read the card's latest comment and answer the one it names.
workflow.refused.loop.staleStep.next.description: The next step after an answer to an earlier design or follow-up (#1382, #1467).

workflow.refused.loop.stepNotHere.messag.defaultMessage: {step, select, followUp {{card} is in {stage}: a follow-up is posted for its check once the work is in review or has passed it.} other {{card} is in {stage}: a design is posted for its check before the work goes to review.}}
workflow.refused.loop.stepNotHere.messag.description: A refused card loop step (#1382, #1467): a design was posted for a card that isn't being worked on (not in Doing), or a follow-up (a change asked of reviewed work, such as a screenshot's) for a card that isn't in Review or Passed. {card} is a card key; {stage} the stage it is in; step (select): followUp, or other for a design. Translate each sentence.

workflow.refused.loop.stepNotHere.next.defaultMessage: {step, select, followUp {Send the work to review, or say it in a comment.} other {Post it while the card is being worked on, or say it in a comment.}}
workflow.refused.loop.stepNotHere.next.description: The next step after a design posted for a card that is not being worked on, or a follow-up for a card not in Review or Passed (#1382, #1467). step (select): followUp, or other for a design. Translate each sentence.

workflow.refused.loop.stepNotYours.messa.defaultMessage: {side, select, builder {Only the builder of {card} posts its design or follow-up, or goes ahead with a design.} other {Only the reviewer of {card} checks its design or follow-up.}}
workflow.refused.loop.stepNotYours.messa.description: A refused card loop step (#1382, #1467): the agent isn't on the side of the loop the step belongs to (a reviewer posting a design or a follow-up, a builder answering its own). A follow-up: a change asked of reviewed work (such as a screenshot's), ready for the reviewer's check. {card} is a card key; side (select): builder or reviewer, whose step it is. Translate each sentence.

workflow.refused.loop.stepNotYours.next.defaultMessage: {side, select, builder {Leave it to the card's builder; a reviewer answers with ok or gaps.} other {Leave it to the card's reviewer; nobody checks their own work.}}
workflow.refused.loop.stepNotYours.next.description: The next step after a refused card loop step from the wrong side (#1382, #1467). side: builder or reviewer, the agent the step belongs to. ok and gaps are the reviewer's answers, as agents name them: keep them as they are.

workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.change.defaultMessage: How long is set in Project Settings → Card loops → Design check wait.
workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.change.description: Where the wait for a design check is changed (#1382). Names of settings: keep them as Combwork shows them.

workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.message.defaultMessage: {card}: its design's check is due in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.message.description: A refused going ahead with a design before its reviewer's check is due (#1382, Card loops → Design check wait). {card} is a card key; {minutes} how many minutes are left.

workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.next.defaultMessage: Wait for the answer; with none by then, go ahead as posted.
workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.next.description: The next step after going ahead with a design too early (#1382).

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ch.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Who merges. A card keeps the rules it started with.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ch.description: Where the rule that Combwork merges cards is changed; a card keeps the rules it started under unless the change is applied to it.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.me.defaultMessage: Combwork merges {card}: agents don't merge it or report its merge.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.me.description: A refused report of a merge, or a claim of the merge slot, for a card whose rules say Combwork merges it (the merge queue). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: Once it is approved, the merge queue merges it and moves it to Done: wait for that, or for it to come back.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card Combwork merges, when it isn't in the merge queue yet.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: The merge queue has merged it already: nothing is left to do.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card Combwork has already merged.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until you resume it; it moves to Done once merged, or comes back.} other {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until it is resumed: wait for Done, or for it to come back.}}
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card in a paused merge queue. {target} is a branch name. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until you answer in For you; it moves to Done once merged, or comes back.} other {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until the user answers in For you: wait for Done, or for it to come back.}}
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card in a merge queue paused for the user's answer (in For you: whether to update the branch now, or how to settle a merge Combwork couldn't finish). {target} is a branch name. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until you fix what stopped it and resume it; it moves to Done once merged, or comes back.} other {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until the user fixes what stopped it and resumes it: wait for Done, or for it to come back.}}
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card in a merge queue paused by something only the user can fix (an error from git, say), then Resume. {target} is a branch name. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until you put right the folder {target} is checked out in and resume it; it moves to Done once merged, or comes back.} other {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until the user puts right the folder {target} is checked out in and resumes it: wait for Done, or for it to come back.}}
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card in a merge queue paused for the folder its branch is checked out in (on another branch, files staged or changed, agents at work there). {target} is a branch name. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which paused while workflow rules were off and moves on once they are enforced again (if they already are, once you resume it); it moves to Done once merged, or comes back.} other {It is in the merge queue for {target}, which paused while workflow rules were off and moves on once they are enforced again (if they already are, once the user resumes it): wait for Done, or for it to come back.}}
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card in a merge queue that paused while the workflow rules were turned off: Combwork resumes it when they are turned on again. {target} is a branch name. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: It is in the merge queue for {target} (position {n, number}) and moves to Done once merged: wait for that, or for it to come back.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card Combwork merges, waiting in the merge queue. {target} is a branch name; {n} its place in the queue (1 is next).

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: It came back from the merge queue: fix it in your worktree, commit and submit again.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card the merge queue returned to its builder (a conflict, failed checks, a hook).

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: Its pass is stale: its line changed since it passed review (it is at {current}). Submit it again for review; it is queued once it passes again.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card Combwork merges, approved but its pass stale: its branch has commits the review didn't cover. {current} is a commit's short hash.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.defaultMessage: The merge queue is merging it into {target} now and moves it to Done once merged: wait for that, or for it to come back.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.description: The next step after a refused merge of a card the merge queue is testing or merging now. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.merge.waitsForBlockers..defaultMessage: {card} depends on {waitsFor}, which isn't Done: it isn't closed as merged before then.
workflow.refused.merge.waitsForBlockers..description: HI-2709: a refused report of a merge: the card depends on {waitsFor} (card keys, comma-joined), which aren't Done yet. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.merge.waitsForBlockers..defaultMessage: Wait for {waitsFor} to be Done, then report the merge again.
workflow.refused.merge.waitsForBlockers..description: HI-2709: the next step after a merge report refused for an unfinished dependency: {waitsFor} are card keys.

workflow.refused.move.doingNobody.messag.defaultMessage: {card} would be in {stage} with nobody on it{also, select, yes {, and the move skips: {rules}} other {}}.
workflow.refused.move.doingNobody.messag.description: A refused move into the Active stage by the Combwork Assistant (HI-2062): the card {card} (its key, like AM-12) would have no agent on it. {stage} is the stage's name. {also} (select): yes when the move also skips other rules, listed in {rules}; translate both branches.

workflow.refused.move.doingNobody.next.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {Choose nobody on it, an agent on it, or an agent started on it.} other {Ask the user which they want: nobody on it (move it again with override and their reason), an agent on it (agent), or an agent started on it (cw_start_task).}}
workflow.refused.move.doingNobody.next.description: The next step after the Assistant's move into Active was refused for leaving nobody on the card: the user chooses nobody on it, an agent given the card, or an agent started on it. override, agent and cw_start_task are names of a call's fields and a tool: keep them as they are. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.chan.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {These rules are set in Version Control, where you can change them.} other {These rules are set in Version Control, where the user can change them.}}
workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.chan.description: Where the rules a move would skip are changed: the project's Version Control tab (a tab name: use it as Combwork shows it). {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.mess.description: A move that skips rules: {rules} lists the rule names.

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.next.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {Moving it anyway needs your reason: one you gave for it, or one you give once told which rules this skips.} other {Move it anyway only with the user's reason. One they gave with their request is enough ("I merged it by hand", say): move it again with override and that reason, in their words. With none, tell them which rules this skips and ask for theirs.}}
workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.next.description: The next step for a move that skips rules (said to the Combwork Assistant): move anyway (an override) only with the user's own reason, given with the request (then the agent moves it at once, HI-2260) or after being told which rules the move skips. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.move.noStage.change.defaultMessage: A project's steps follow its options in Version Control.
workflow.refused.move.noStage.change.description: Where the stages a project has are set: its Version Control options (a tab name: use it as Combwork shows it).

workflow.refused.move.noStage.message.defaultMessage: {card} can't go to {stage}: this project's rules have no such step.
workflow.refused.move.noStage.message.description: A refused move: the card was moved to a board stage the project's workflow rules don't have (Review with no review, say). {card} is a card key, {stage} a stage name.

workflow.refused.move.noStage.next.defaultMessage: Move it to one of its steps: {stages}.
workflow.refused.move.noStage.next.description: The next step after a move to a stage the rules lack: the stages they have. {stages} lists stage names.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.messag.defaultMessage: {card} is in {stage}: {move} isn't possible from there.
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.messag.description: A refused intent: not possible from the stage the card is in. {stage} is a stage name, {move} the intent.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.next.description: The next step: the intents possible from the stage. {moves} lists them.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextBu.defaultMessage: It waits for its reviewer's verdict: wait for that, which brings it back if there is more to do.
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextBu.description: The next step after a card's builder was refused a move while the card waits in Review for its reviewer (#1604): the review's verdict comes first. Read by agents and shown in the window alike: it names no one.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextBu.defaultMessage: A change asked for while it is in Review, committed: submit it again with followUp: true, which keeps it in Review for its reviewer to check. Anything else waits for its reviewer's verdict.
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextBu.description: The next step after a card's builder submitted it again while it waits in Review (HI-1832): the verdict comes first, but a change the reviewer asked for is submitted as a follow-up. followUp is the tool's option, as agents type it: keep it as it is. Read by agents and shown in the window alike: it names no one.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextDo.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {It's finished. More work on it that you ask for takes it back to Doing; separate follow-up work goes on a new card.} other {It's finished. More work on it that the user asked for: move it back with cw_update_task (column: doing), then work on it as usual. Separate follow-up work goes on a new card (cw_create_task).}}
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextDo.description: The next step after an agent's start or submit was refused on a card in Done (HI-2227): more work on that card the user asked for moves it back to Doing; separate follow-up work is a new card. cw_update_task, cw_create_task and column: doing are a tool, its argument and value: keep them as they are. Doing is a column name: use it as Combwork shows it. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextNo.defaultMessage: Nothing waits to be done there now.
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextNo.description: The next step after a refused move when nothing is possible from the card's stage (the request it answered is no longer open).

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextRe.defaultMessage: {back, select, yes {Its review is over: it went back for more work. Leave it where it is, with no verdict, and wait for it to come back to Review.} other {Its review is over: it has moved on from Review. Leave it where it is, with no verdict.}}
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.nextRe.description: The next step after a reviewer's review or verdict was refused because the card is no longer in Review (#1604): its review ended. back (select): yes when the card went back to be worked on (Todo or Active), other when it moved on (approved, merged). Review is a stage name: use it as Combwork shows it. Read by agents and shown in the window alike: it names no one. Translate each sentence.

workflow.refused.move.useIntent.message.defaultMessage: Agents don't move cards between columns.
workflow.refused.move.useIntent.message.description: A refused column move by an agent: agents act by intent.

workflow.refused.move.useIntent.next.description: The next step after a refused column move: {intent} is the intent to use.

workflow.refused.paths.excluded.message.defaultMessage: {card}: {path} is in {folder}, which a project without version control leaves out of its work.
workflow.refused.paths.excluded.message.description: A refused declaration of a card's paths (#1511): in a project without version control (None), a card's paths are the files of its work; {path} is under {folder} (node_modules, .venv, .git, .combwork or a folder the project excludes), which never counts as work. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.paths.excluded.next.defaultMessage: Declare only the files of the work, outside {folder}: a card's paths narrow the project's work, never widen it.
workflow.refused.paths.excluded.next.description: The next step after a refused declaration of a card's paths: name files outside the excluded folder {folder} (#1511).

workflow.refused.platform.changed.messag.defaultMessage: {card} can't start under these rules: its project uses {platform} now.
workflow.refused.platform.changed.messag.description: HI-2799: a refused start: the start was prepared under the project’s previous version control, and the project was switched meanwhile. {card} is a card key; {platform} is None, Git or jj.

workflow.refused.platform.changed.next.defaultMessage: Start it again: it is then checked under {platform}’s rules.
workflow.refused.platform.changed.next.description: HI-2799: the next step after a start refused because the project switched version control meanwhile. {platform} is None, Git or jj.

workflow.refused.platform.jjRefused.mess.defaultMessage: {why, select, tooLarge {{card}: jj left {count, plural, one {a new file} other {# new files}} out of its snapshot for being over its size limit for new files (snapshot.max-new-file-size), so the work isn't all recorded: {files}.} mergeWorkingCopy {{card}: the slot's working copy has more than one parent, so its work isn't one line of commits.} notFromBase {{card}: the work in its slot doesn't start from the card's base {base}.} otherCard {{card}: commit {commit} is {other}'s work.} divergent {{card}: commit {commit} is divergent in jj (its change has more than one visible commit).} conflicted {{card}: commit {commit} has unresolved conflicts.} tooLong {{card}: its work has more than {max, number} commits.} unbound {{card}: its slot isn't prepared for this card any more.} isolated {{card}: jj projects have no check copies yet.} recovered {{card}: commits of its work hold copies that Recover… wrote beside the original files: {files}.} other {{card}: jj refused it.}}
workflow.refused.platform.jjRefused.mess.description: HI-2868: a refused move on a card of a project using jj (Jujutsu): why its work can't be taken as it is. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {commit} and {base} are short commit ids; {other} is another card's key; {max} is a number; {files} is a list of file paths and {count} their number (HI-2973). 'working copy', 'divergent' and 'snapshot' are jj's terms; snapshot.max-new-file-size is jj's setting: keep it as it is. Translate each sentence. recovered (HI-2996): Recover… (a button of a stale slot, as the window names it) wrote a copy of the user's version beside a file that had changed meanwhile, and commits of the card's work hold that copy; {files} is a list of file paths, as they are.

workflow.refused.platform.jjRefused.next.defaultMessage: {why, select, tooLarge {Leave a file out deliberately with .gitignore, or raise jj's limit (jj config set --repo snapshot.max-new-file-size and a size in bytes) and commit it with jj commit, then submit again.} mergeWorkingCopy {Commit the work with jj commit, so the working copy is empty on one parent, then submit again.} notFromBase {Rebase the work onto the card's base, or start the card again.} otherCard {Leave that card's commits out of this card's work (rebase without them), then submit again.} divergent {Resolve the divergence in jj (abandon or rewrite one side), then try again.} conflicted {Resolve the conflicts in jj, then try again.} tooLong {Squash some of the commits, then submit again.} unbound {Put the card back and start it again.} isolated {Run the check again without --isolated, in the card's slot.} recovered {Compare each copy with its original and keep what you want under the original name, then take the copies out of every commit of the work (jj squash or jj diffedit: deleting them in a later commit leaves them in its history) and submit again.} other {Look at the slot with jj, then try again.}}
workflow.refused.platform.jjRefused.next.description: HI-2868: the next step after a refused move on a jj project's card, by the reason (why, select). jj commit, --isolated, .gitignore and jj config set --repo snapshot.max-new-file-size are commands and names: keep them as they are. 'working copy' and 'divergent' are jj's terms. Translate each sentence. recovered (HI-2996): copies Recover… wrote beside the originals are in commits of the card's work: the user's version of each is compared with the original, kept under the original name if wanted, and the copies taken out of every commit (jj squash and jj diffedit are commands: keep them).

workflow.refused.platform.switching.mess.defaultMessage: {card} can't start now: its repository's version control is being switched.
workflow.refused.platform.switching.mess.description: HI-2799: a refused start: the project’s repository is switching between Git and jj, and nothing starts on it meanwhile. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.platform.switching.next.defaultMessage: Try again in a moment, once the switch has finished.
workflow.refused.platform.switching.next.description: HI-2799: the next step after a start refused while the repository’s version control is switched.

workflow.refused.platform.targetGone.mes.defaultMessage: {card} was started on {target}, which no longer exists in this repository.
workflow.refused.platform.targetGone.mes.description: HI-2753: a refused move (a submit): the branch the card was started on and merges into (its target, {target}) was deleted, as an integration branch is once it has been merged. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.platform.targetGone.nex.defaultMessage: The user or the Assistant can move it to another branch with its work kept: set its Merges into, or retarget Work merges into.
workflow.refused.platform.targetGone.nex.description: HI-2753: the next step when the branch a card started on is gone: the user or the Combwork Assistant moves the card to another branch (its Merges into, or a retarget after changing Work merges into). Merges into and Work merges into are names in the window: as translated there.

workflow.refused.platform.unknown.messag.defaultMessage: {card}: Combwork couldn't read {what}, so the rule {rule} can't be checked.
workflow.refused.platform.unknown.messag.description: A refused move: a fact a rule needs could not be read (git missing, folder gone). {what} says what, {rule} the rule id.

workflow.refused.platform.unknown.next.defaultMessage: Check Provider Setup or the folder, then try again.
workflow.refused.platform.unknown.next.description: The next step when Combwork could not read what a rule needs.

workflow.refused.platform.unknown.nextGo.defaultMessage: {reader, select, you {The project's Git repository is gone: restore it, or switch the project to None in its Version Control tab (from the next card).} other {The project's Git repository is gone: ask the user to restore it, or to switch the project to None in its Version Control tab (from the next card).}}
workflow.refused.platform.unknown.nextGo.description: The next step when a card was refused because its Git repository was removed or moved: the user restores it, or switches the project to None (no version control) in the Version Control tab, which applies to cards started after. Read by agents and shown in the window. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.queue.advancing.message.defaultMessage: {card} is being merged into {target} now: it can no longer be taken out of the merge queue.
workflow.refused.queue.advancing.message.description: A refused Remove from queue: the merge queue has begun moving the target to the card's merge (it finishes even after a restart). {card} is a card key, {target} a branch name.

workflow.refused.queue.advancing.next.defaultMessage: Wait for the merge to finish. If the change isn't wanted, revert it in {target}.
workflow.refused.queue.advancing.next.description: The next step after a refused Remove from queue while the card is being merged. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.change.defaultMessage: Retry merge on the merge queue retries it once.
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.change.description: Who can override a refused requeue: the user, with Retry merge on the merge queue (glossary 2.5: merge queue).

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.message.defaultMessage: {card} at {revision} can't go back into the merge queue unchanged: {why}
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.message.description: A refused resubmission into the merge queue. {card} is a card key, {revision} a short revision id, {why} one of the requeue reasons below, a whole sentence.

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.next.defaultMessage: Fix the failure, commit and submit the new revision.
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.next.description: The next step after a refused unchanged requeue.

workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.defaultMessage: {card} has a decision you haven't read.
workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.description: A refused review or verdict: the card has a newer decision than the reviewer has received.

workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.defaultMessage: Read it, judge whether the work meets it, then give your verdict.
workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.description: The next step after a refused verdict for an unread decision.

workflow.refused.review.headMoved.messag.defaultMessage: {card}'s line has moved since it was submitted: it was submitted at {submitted}, and its head is now {head}, a different change. A pass covers only the revision submitted.
workflow.refused.review.headMoved.messag.description: A refused passing verdict (HI-1763): the card's branch has new commits since the revision under review (a follow-up, say). {card} is the card's key; {submitted} and {head} are commits' short hashes.

workflow.refused.review.headMoved.next.defaultMessage: A commit you asked for: ask its builder to submit {head} as a follow-up (cw_request_builder), which keeps it in Review with no round counted, then start your review again. Otherwise give a failing verdict saying so (cw_verdict, pass: false), and its builder submits it as the next round.
workflow.refused.review.headMoved.next.description: The next step after a pass refused because the branch moved on (HI-1763, HI-1832): a commit the reviewer asked for is submitted by the builder as a follow-up (the card stays in Review, no round counted) and reviewed again; any other is failed so the builder submits it as a new round. {head} is a commit's short hash; keep the tool names and the argument as they are.

workflow.refused.review.inProgress.chang.defaultMessage: Only the user takes a review over; one whose reviewer has left the project or stopped is free again.
workflow.refused.review.inProgress.chang.description: Who can take over a review in progress (HI-2487): only the user; it is free again once its reviewer agent is removed from the project or its session has stopped.

workflow.refused.review.inProgress.messa.defaultMessage: {who, select, user {The user is reviewing {card}'s submission {submission}} other {{reviewer} is reviewing {card}'s submission {submission}}}, and has been for {minutes, plural, =0 {less than a minute} one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
workflow.refused.review.inProgress.messa.description: A refused start of a review (HI-2487): someone else started reviewing the same submission and hasn't given its verdict. {who}: user (the user reviews it) or agent (another reviewer agent, named by {reviewer}, its name). {card} is a card key like AM-12, {submission} the submission's number, {minutes} how long ago its review started (select: translate each branch).

workflow.refused.review.inProgress.next.defaultMessage: {who, select, user {Leave it to the user} other {Leave it to {reviewer}}}: don't review {card} or give it a verdict.
workflow.refused.review.inProgress.next.description: The next step after a review refused because someone else is reviewing the card (HI-2487). {who}: user (the user reviews it) or agent (another reviewer agent, named by {reviewer}). {card} is a card key (select: translate each branch).

workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.mes.description: A refused review: the card has no submission.

workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.nex.defaultMessage: Wait for its builder to submit it.
workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.nex.description: The next step when there is nothing to review.

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.change.defaultMessage: Only Move anyway, on the card, skips this rule.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.change.description: Who can override the no-self-review rule: only the user, moving the card anyway (glossary 2.4: override, Move anyway).

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.messag.defaultMessage: You worked on {card}, so you can't review it.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.messag.description: A refused review: the reviewer is one of the agents who built the card.

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.next.defaultMessage: Leave the review to another reviewer.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.next.description: The next step after a refused self-review.

workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged.
workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.description: Where the rule that refused starting a card before the cards it waits for are done is changed.
A refused start of a card. {card} and {waitsFor} are card keys (AM-12): the card waits for {waitsFor}'s work to be merged or accepted.

workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.defaultMessage: Wait for {waitsFor} to be done, or work on another card.
workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.description: The next step after a refused start: {waitsFor} is the card key it waits for.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.change.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done.
workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.change.description: Where the rule that refused starting a blocked card is changed.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.messag.description: A refused start of a card. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {reason} is why the card is blocked, in the words given.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.next.defaultMessage: Wait for it to be unblocked, or work on another card.
workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.next.description: The next step after a refused start of a blocked card.

workflow.refused.start.platformReady.mes.defaultMessage: {card} can't start: cards don't run in a jj project yet.
workflow.refused.start.platformReady.mes.description: A refused start of a card in a project using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799): Combwork shows its repository but doesn’t start card work there yet. {card} is a card key. Keep jj (the tool’s name).

workflow.refused.start.platformReady.nex.defaultMessage: Work on it outside Combwork’s cards, or switch the project to Git in Version Control.
workflow.refused.start.platformReady.nex.description: The next step after a refused start in a jj project (HI-2799). Version Control is the tab’s name (glossary 2.1). Keep Git and jj.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.cha.defaultMessage: This is set in Version Control → Where cards are built.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.cha.description: Where the rule that refused starting for want of a slot is changed.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.mes.defaultMessage: {card} can't start: no slot is free.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.mes.description: A refused start: every working folder (slot) is lent to other work. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.nex.defaultMessage: Wait for a slot to be free.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.nex.description: The next step after a refused start for want of a slot.

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.cha.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Checks pass before review.
workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.cha.description: Where the rule that refused a submit for a missing check is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.mes.defaultMessage: Review refused: {check} hasn't passed on {revision}.{why, select, notCheck { Its last run passed but didn't count: it wasn't the check's configured command.} notContained { Its last run passed but didn't count: what it ran on doesn't contain the revision.} dirty { Its last run passed but didn't count: the folder had uncommitted changes{files, select, none {} other { ({files})}}.} moved { Its last run passed but didn't count: something else was checked out by its end.} changed { Its last run passed but didn't count: files changed in the folder while it ran{files, select, none {} other { ({files})}}.} revisionChanged { Its last run passed but didn't count: the card's files changed while it ran.} other {}}
workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.mes.description: A refused submit: a configured check has no passing counted run on the revision. {check} is the check name, {revision} a short revision id. {why} picks why its last run there didn't count (#1654; keep each branch's key as it is; 'other': it didn't run there, or failed, and nothing is added); {files} lists the paths that changed, or is 'none' (keep the key).

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.nex.defaultMessage: {why, select, dirty {Commit or remove the uncommitted changes, run {command} again, then submit again.} changed {{copy, select, yes {Run {command} again with nothing else writing in the folder, or add --isolated to run it in a check copy of its own, then submit again.} other {Run {command} again with nothing else writing in the folder, then submit again.}}} notContained {Run {command} in the card's own folder, at its revision, then submit again.} other {Run {command}, then submit again.}}
workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.nex.description: The next step after a refused submit for a missing check: {command} is the command to run. {why} picks the remedy for why its last run didn't count (#1654; keep each branch's key as it is); {copy} is 'yes' where a check copy (--isolated, kept as typed) can be used.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.change.defaultMessage: This rule comes with review and merging in Version Control.
workflow.refused.submit.clean.change.description: Where the rule that refused a submit with uncommitted changes comes from.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.message.defaultMessage: {card} can't go to review: {folder} has uncommitted changes ({files}).
workflow.refused.submit.clean.message.description: A refused submit: the working folder has uncommitted changes. {folder} is a folder path, {files} a list of file paths.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.next.defaultMessage: Commit the card's changes, then submit for review again; if you were asked only to submit it (not to do the card), ask the user before committing. Changes that aren't the card's: ask before removing them.
workflow.refused.submit.clean.next.description: The next step after a refused submit for review with uncommitted changes (HI-1618, HI-2227, HI-2257): an agent doing the card commits its work; one asked only to submit it asks the user before committing; changes that aren't the card's are removed only once asked about.

workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.defaultMessage: {card} has a decision or a comment from the user that you haven't seen.
workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.description: A refused submit (HI-2854): the card has a decision, or a comment the user wrote, newer than the builder has received.

workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.defaultMessage: Check your work against each (listed below, or read the card), then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.description: The next step after a refused submit for an unseen decision or comment of the user's: the agent's reply lists them below when it can.

workflow.refused.submit.empty.message.description: A refused submit for review: the card's line has no commit since it started (git's words: nothing committed). {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.submit.empty.messageFor.defaultMessage: Nothing is committed to review yet.
workflow.refused.submit.empty.messageFor.description: A refused move of a card to Review by the user (a drag on the board): the card's line has no commit since it started. Shown under a title that names the card and the column, so it doesn't name them.

workflow.refused.submit.empty.next.defaultMessage: {changes, select, yes {Commit the card's work, then submit for review again; if you were asked only to submit it (not to do the card), ask the user before committing.} none {Its folder has no changes either. A card that needs none (it only runs or checks something, or its work is already there) is no-code: ask for that with cw_ask_user (action noCode), or cw_ask_assistant where it's already decided. Otherwise make its change, commit it and submit again.} other {Commit the card's work, then submit for review again; if you were asked only to submit it (not to do the card), ask the user before committing. A card that needs no change is no-code: ask for that with cw_ask_user (action noCode).}}
workflow.refused.submit.empty.next.description: The next step after a refused submit for review with nothing committed (HI-2227, HI-2257). {changes} (select): yes when the card's folder has uncommitted changes (an agent doing the card commits them; one asked only to submit it asks the user first), none when it has none (a card needing no change is made no-code by the user, asked with the tools named), other when unknown. cw_ask_user, cw_ask_assistant and noCode are names of tools and an option: keep them as they are; translate each branch's whole sentences.

workflow.refused.submit.empty.nextForUse.defaultMessage: Commit the card's work, then move it again.
workflow.refused.submit.empty.nextForUse.description: The next step after the user's move of a card to Review was refused with nothing committed: commit the work, then move the card again.

workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.ch.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Each card’s focused tests.
workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.ch.description: Where the rule that refused a submit for focused tests (G20) is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.me.defaultMessage: Review refused: {card}'s focused tests couldn't be chosen for {revision}: {state, select, tooBroad {its project's picker says the change needs every test.} other {{why, select, noPicker {the project has no picker.} timedOut {its project's picker took too long.} badOutput {its project's picker gave output Combwork can't read.} tooMany {its project's picker named too many tests.} moved {its folder moved to another revision while the picker ran.} dirty {its folder had uncommitted changes.} changed {files changed in its folder while the picker ran.} noChange {its change couldn't be read.} other {its project's picker failed.}}}}
workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.me.description: A refused submit (G20, HI-1367): the tests the card's change needs couldn't be chosen. {card} is its key, {revision} a short commit id; {state} and {why} pick the reason (keep each branch's key as it is).

workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.ne.defaultMessage: Name the tests the change needs with tests on submit, for the reviewer to check, or fix what stopped the picker, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.ne.description: The next step after a refused submit for focused tests (G20), addressed to the agent: tests is the submit tool’s argument, kept as typed.

workflow.refused.submit.followUpNotBuild.defaultMessage: {card}'s follow-up is its builder's to submit: you aren't building it.
workflow.refused.submit.followUpNotBuild.description: A refused follow-up submission (HI-1832: a commit its reviewer asked for, submitted while the card is in Review): only the agent building the card submits one. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.submit.followUpNotBuild.defaultMessage: Leave it to its builder, or say what you found in a comment.
workflow.refused.submit.followUpNotBuild.description: The next step after a follow-up submission refused because the agent is not the card's builder (HI-1832).

workflow.refused.submit.identity.change.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Commits use the project's identity.
workflow.refused.submit.identity.change.description: Where the identity rule is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.identity.message.defaultMessage: {missing, select, yes {{card} can't be submitted: its commits must use the project's identity, and git has none set for the project.} other {{card}: commit {commit} isn't authored with the project's identity ({email}).}}
workflow.refused.submit.identity.message.description: A refused submit: a commit's author email isn't the project's, as git config has it now. {missing} (select; keep the keys): yes when git has no identity (name and email) for the project at all. {commit} is a short commit id, {email} the project's email address.

workflow.refused.submit.identity.next.defaultMessage: {missing, select, yes {Set the project's identity in Version Control → Branches & remotes → Commit identity (or with {command}), then submit again.} other {Set the identity, run {command}, then submit again.}}
workflow.refused.submit.identity.next.description: The next step after a refused submit for a commit's identity: {command} is the git command to use (kept as typed). {missing} (select; keep the keys): yes when git has no identity for the project; Version Control → Branches & remotes → Commit identity is where Combwork's window sets it (use the names Combwork shows for the tab, its section and heading).

workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.mes.defaultMessage: {card} is already submitted at {revision} and waits for review or merging.
workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.mes.description: A refused submit: the same revision is already waiting. {card} is a card key, {revision} a short revision id.

workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.nex.defaultMessage: Wait for its review or merge.
workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.nex.description: The next step after a refused duplicate submission.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.c.defaultMessage: This rule is set in Version Control → Agents stop what they started before review.
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.c.description: Where the rule about stopping runs before review is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.m.defaultMessage: {card}: runs you started are still going ({runs}).
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.m.description: A refused submit: the agent still has runs going. {runs} lists their titles.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.n.defaultMessage: Stop them or let them finish, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.n.description: The next step after a refused submit while runs are going.

workflow.refused.submit.ready.message.description: A refused submit: the revision stores conflicts. {files} lists file paths.

workflow.refused.submit.ready.next.defaultMessage: Resolve the conflicts, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.ready.next.description: The next step after a refused submit of a conflicted revision.

workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.description: A refused submit: the same revision again without a note.

workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.defaultMessage: Submit it again with a note saying what changed in your answer, or commit a new revision.
workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.description: The next step when submitting a reviewed revision again.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.change.defaultMessage: Each card in its own folder needs no trailers: Version Control → Where cards are built.
workflow.refused.submit.trailer.change.description: Where the setting that needs commit trailers is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.message.defaultMessage: {card}: commit {commit} has no card trailer, and another card's agent works in this folder.
workflow.refused.submit.trailer.message.description: A refused submit in a shared folder: a commit lacks the Combwork-Card trailer. {commit} is a short commit id.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.next.defaultMessage: {at, select, head {Run {command}, then submit again.} other {Other commits follow it, so amending or rebasing would rewrite them, other agents' work among them: do neither. Report it with cw_cannot_within_rules (rule submit.trailer), and the user decides.}}
workflow.refused.submit.trailer.next.description: The next step after a refused submit for a missing trailer (HI-2562). {at} (select): head when the commit is the folder's newest, so amending it is safe; other when commits follow it. {command} is the git command to run, kept as typed; cw_cannot_within_rules is a tool's name, kept as typed.

workflow.refused.submit.unchanged.messag.defaultMessage: {card}: its files haven't changed since it started.
workflow.refused.submit.unchanged.messag.description: A refused submit for review in a project with no version control: none of the card's files changed. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.submit.unchanged.next.defaultMessage: Change the card's files, then submit it for review.
workflow.refused.submit.unchanged.next.description: The next step after a refused submit for review in a project with no version control, nothing changed.

workflow.refused.verdict.currentSubmissi.description: A refused verdict: it names an older submission. {submission} is its number.
The next step after a verdict on an old submission: {latest} is the latest submission number.

workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.messa.defaultMessage: You haven't started a review of {card}'s submission {submission}.
workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.messa.description: A refused verdict: the reviewer never started reviewing that submission. {submission} is its number.

workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.next.defaultMessage: Start the review first, then give your verdict.
workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.next.description: The next step after a verdict without a started review.

workflow.refused.why.passes.defaultMessage: {n, number} of {q, plural, one {# reviewer} other {# reviewers}} passed it.
workflow.refused.why.passes.description: The {why} of a refused merge: not enough distinct reviewers passed the revision. {n} and {q} are numbers.

workflow.refused.why.requeueLimit.defaultMessage: it was sent back unchanged {n, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} already.
workflow.refused.why.requeueLimit.description: The {why} of a refused requeue: the limit of unchanged requeues was reached. {n} is how many.

workflow.refused.why.requeueNotTransient.defaultMessage: its last merge failed for a reason in the work (a conflict, red checks or a hook), which needs a new revision.
workflow.refused.why.requeueNotTransient.description: The {why} of a refused requeue: the merge failure wasn't transient. Starts lower case: it follows a colon.

workflow.refused.why.stale.description: The {why} of a refused merge or requeue: the revision's pass no longer holds.

workflow.refused.why.userOk.defaultMessage: it waits for the OK before merging.
workflow.refused.why.userOk.description: The {why} of a refused merge: the user's approval is missing.

workflow.roundChoice.defaultMessage: {choice, select, carryOn {Carry on} split {Split it} accept {Accept with follow-ups} takeOver {Take it over} other {{choice}}}
workflow.roundChoice.description: One of the user's four choices when a card reaches its card loop's round limit: carry on with more review rounds, split the card into smaller ones, accept the work as it is with follow-up cards, or take the work over themselves. Translate each choice; keep the codes before the braces.

workflow.rule.approval.given.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G10).

workflow.rule.card.kind.defaultMessage: A card's kind is set when it is made
workflow.rule.card.kind.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a change skips it: a card is code or no code (a decision, a write-up, a trial) from when it is made; changing it later is an exception the user makes (glossary: override).

workflow.rule.done.contained.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: a card is done only when its work is in its target (glossary 2.6: G5).

workflow.rule.integrate.approved.defaultMessage: Work is reviewed before it's merged
workflow.rule.integrate.approved.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G1).

workflow.rule.integrate.checksPassed.defaultMessage: Checks pass on the merged result
workflow.rule.integrate.checksPassed.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G9).

workflow.rule.integrate.upToDate.defaultMessage: Work is up to date before it merges
workflow.rule.integrate.upToDate.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G8, without the branch name).

workflow.rule.move.doingNobody.defaultMessage: A card in Active has someone on it, unless you say otherwise
workflow.rule.move.doingNobody.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips it (HI-2062): the Combwork Assistant moves a card into Active with nobody on it only with the user's reason (glossary: override). Active is a stage's name.

workflow.rule.requeue.allowed.defaultMessage: Unchanged work is queued again only after a failure outside it
workflow.rule.requeue.allowed.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: work goes back into the merge queue unchanged only after a merge failed for a reason outside the work (a network error, a timeout).

workflow.rule.review.decisionsReceived.defaultMessage: The reviewer has read every decision
workflow.rule.review.decisionsReceived.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.5: reviewer).

workflow.rule.review.inProgress.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move can't check it (HI-2487): a reviewer agent doesn't start a review another reviewer is still doing; only the user takes one over.

workflow.rule.review.notAuthor.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N2, G2).

workflow.rule.start.dependenciesIntegrat.defaultMessage: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done
workflow.rule.start.dependenciesIntegrat.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N6, G14).

workflow.rule.start.notBlocked.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.start.platformReady.defaultMessage: Cards run only where Combwork supports the version control
workflow.rule.start.platformReady.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can’t check it (HI-2799): cards don’t start in a project using jj (Jujutsu) yet.

workflow.rule.start.slotAvailable.defaultMessage: Each card in its own folder
workflow.rule.start.slotAvailable.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G11 values): a card starts only when a folder is free.

workflow.rule.submit.checksPassed.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N3, G3).

workflow.rule.submit.clean.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.submit.decisionsReceived.defaultMessage: The builder has seen every decision and every comment of the user's
workflow.rule.submit.decisionsReceived.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: the agent who built the card has seen every decision on it, and every comment the user wrote (HI-2854; glossary 2.5: builder).

workflow.rule.submit.focusedChosen.defaultMessage: Each card’s focused tests are chosen before review
workflow.rule.submit.focusedChosen.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can’t check it (G20, HI-1367): the tests a card’s change needs are chosen, or named by its builder, when it is submitted.

workflow.rule.submit.identity.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G12).

workflow.rule.submit.notDuplicate.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: the same revision isn't submitted twice.

workflow.rule.submit.ownRunsStopped.defaultMessage: Agents stop what they started before review
workflow.rule.submit.ownRunsStopped.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G13).

workflow.rule.submit.ready.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.submit.trailer.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: in a shared folder, each commit names its card.

workflow.rule.verdict.currentSubmission.defaultMessage: A verdict is on the latest submission
workflow.rule.verdict.currentSubmission.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.rule.verdict.reviewing.description: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: a reviewer starts a review before giving a verdict (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.slots.archive.description: A setting under “Slots and copies”: the command Combwork runs in a slot before removing it.

workflow.slots.archiveDesc.defaultMessage: Runs in a slot before Combwork removes it. If it fails, the slot is kept.
workflow.slots.archiveDesc.description: What the setting “Archive script” does (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.slots.branches.description: A link from “Slots in use and ready” to the Version Control tab’s Branches & remotes section, where each slot’s line is (its name as translated there).

workflow.slots.carried.defaultMessage: {agent}’s old worktree, finishing its current work
workflow.slots.carried.description: What a slot holds, in the list under “Slots and copies”: an agent’s worktree from before 1.0, kept for it until its current card or lane ends (#1441). {agent} is its name.

workflow.slots.copiesDefault.description: The placeholder of the setting “Review and check copies” while it isn’t set: the number Combwork keeps.

workflow.slots.copiesNow.defaultMessage: {n, plural, =0 {No copies yet.} one {# copy now, {leased, number} in use.} other {# copies now, {leased, number} in use.}}
workflow.slots.copiesNow.description: Under the setting “Review and check copies”: how many copies the project has now, and how many are leased.

workflow.slots.copiesSize.description: A setting under “Slots and copies”: how many review and check copies the project keeps (glossary 2.5: review copy).

workflow.slots.copiesSizeDesc.defaultMessage: How many copies the project keeps, each at exactly one revision, for reviewers and isolated checks. Empty keeps the larger of two and its reviewers plus one. They use the setup script.
workflow.slots.copiesSizeDesc.description: What the setting “Review and check copies” does (glossary 2.5: review copy; isolated checks: cw-progress --check --isolated).

workflow.slots.copy.description: A setting under “Slots and copies”: the git-ignored files copied from the project folder into each new slot.

workflow.slots.copyDesc.defaultMessage: Git-ignored files copied from the project folder into each new slot, one pattern per line, such as .env files.
workflow.slots.copyDesc.description: What the setting “Files copied into new slots” does (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.slots.desc.defaultMessage: These are saved as you change them, apart from the options above.
workflow.slots.desc.description: Under the heading “Slots and copies”: its settings save at once, unlike the workflow options, which are saved with Save….

workflow.slots.fromSetup.defaultMessage: From the project’s setup command before 1.0
workflow.slots.fromSetup.description: Where the setting “Setup script” comes from while it isn’t set: the setup command the project had for agents’ worktrees before 1.0.

workflow.slots.gitFiles.description: A switch under “Slots and copies” (HI-1182): whether Combwork checks out the repository’s submodules and fetches its Git LFS files in each slot and copy it makes. Keep LFS (Git LFS, a product’s name).

workflow.slots.gitFilesDesc.defaultMessage: Before the setup script, checks out submodules and fetches Git LFS files in each new slot, in each review and check copy, and in the merge queue’s folder. Without it, they have empty submodule folders and LFS pointer files.
workflow.slots.gitFilesDesc.description: What the switch “Set up submodules and LFS” does (HI-1182; glossary 2.5: slot, review copy). Keep Git LFS (a product’s name); pointer files are the small text files Git LFS keeps in place of the real ones.

workflow.slots.gitFilesLfs.description: Under the switch “Set up submodules and LFS” (HI-1182): the project uses Git LFS, and git-lfs is installed. {version} is git-lfs’s own version line, such as git-lfs/3.8.1 (GitHub; windows amd64; go 1.27.3). Keep Git LFS.

workflow.slots.gitFilesNoFilter.defaultMessage: It uses Git LFS, but it isn’t set up for this repository: slots and copies can’t be prepared until you run git lfs install.
workflow.slots.gitFilesNoFilter.description: Under the switch “Set up submodules and LFS” (HI-1182): git-lfs is installed but its filter isn’t configured, so LFS files would stay pointer files. Keep Git LFS and the command git lfs install as they are.

workflow.slots.gitFilesNoLfs.defaultMessage: It uses Git LFS, but git-lfs isn’t installed: slots and copies can’t be prepared until it is. Turning this off skips the step, but where your git config requires the LFS filter, git itself still can’t check files out.
workflow.slots.gitFilesNoLfs.description: Under the switch “Set up submodules and LFS” (HI-1182): the project uses Git LFS and the git-lfs program can’t be found. Keep Git LFS and git-lfs (a product and its program).

workflow.slots.gitFilesSubmodules.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {This project has # submodule.} other {This project has # submodules.}}
workflow.slots.gitFilesSubmodules.description: Under the switch “Set up submodules and LFS” (HI-1182): how many submodules the project folder’s repository has.

workflow.slots.heading.description: A heading of the Version Control tab’s Workflow section (Git): the project’s slots (worktrees Combwork lends to cards and lanes) and its review and check copies (glossary 2.5: slot, review copy).

workflow.slots.held.defaultMessage: Held by an ended session of agent {agent}
workflow.slots.held.description: In the list of slots (Version Control → Slots and copies): the agent's ({agent}) last session there has ended, but Combwork doesn't know that everything it started has, so nothing else uses the slot until it is released (#1506). A noun before the name (glossary §1 rule 4).

workflow.slots.inUse.description: A read-only list under “Slots and copies”: the project’s slots, what each is lent to, and those ready (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.slots.inherit.description: A button beside a slot setting set for this project: stop setting it here, and use the inherited value again (the workspace’s, Combwork’s or the default).

workflow.slots.lentCard.description: What a slot is lent to, in the list under “Slots and copies”: the builder agent {agent} (its name) for the card {card} (its key, HI-12).

workflow.slots.lentLane.description: What a slot is lent to, in the list under “Slots and copies”: the builder agent {agent} (its name) for its lane (glossary: lane).

workflow.slots.levelInherit.description: A button beside a slot default set at this level (Settings → Workflow defaults or Settings → Workspace): stop setting it here, and use the inherited value (Combwork’s, or the default).

workflow.slots.levelNone.description: Where a slot default’s value comes from, in Settings → Workflow defaults or Settings → Workspace: this level sets it to nothing (no files are copied), over the value it would inherit.

workflow.slots.noSlots.defaultMessage: No slots yet: one is made when a card starts.
workflow.slots.noSlots.description: Under “Slots in use and ready” when the project has no slot yet.

workflow.slots.none.description: A slot script that isn’t set: nothing runs.

workflow.slots.notRecovered.defaultMessage: {slot} wasn’t recovered: {why, select, busy {something works in it (an agent working there: stop it first)} preparing {its card is still being prepared there} notStale {it isn’t stale any more} identity {its folder isn’t the workspace Combwork made} other {jj couldn’t do it}}.
workflow.slots.notRecovered.description: A notice after recovering a stale jj slot was refused (HI-2869, HI-2913). {why} picks the reason: busy (something works in the slot, such as the agent of the lane holding it, which the user stops first), preparing (the card the slot is lent to is still being prepared there), and the others. Keep the select keys.

workflow.slots.openAdvanced.description: A button beside “Reviewers review in review copies”: opens Settings → Advanced.

workflow.slots.recover.description: A button beside a stale jj slot (HI-2869): brings it up to date, keeping any edits jj hadn’t recorded (asks first).

workflow.slots.recoverMessage.defaultMessage: Combwork copies any edits jj hadn’t recorded in it aside first, into the folder below, then brings the slot up to date with jj. It runs only while nothing works in the slot.
workflow.slots.recoverMessage.description: The confirmation before recovering a stale jj slot (HI-2869); the folder edits are copied into is listed under it.

workflow.slots.recoverTitle.description: The title of the confirmation before recovering a stale jj slot (HI-2869). {slot} is the slot’s name.

workflow.slots.recovered.description: A notice after a stale jj slot was recovered (HI-2869).

workflow.slots.recoveredAsides.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {# file was created again during the recovery, so the version it had before was left beside it: {files}.} other {# files were created again during the recovery, so the version each had before was left beside it: {files}.}} Keep what you want of it, then delete it.
workflow.slots.recoveredAsides.description: HI-2996: after a stale jj slot was recovered: while it put files back, something created some of them again, so Combwork left the version the file had just before (moved aside) under another name beside it. {files} lists their full paths, joined as a list. The user keeps what they want and deletes that copy.

workflow.slots.recoveredCopies.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {# file had changed meanwhile, so your version of it was written beside it, under the name below.} other {# files had changed meanwhile, so your version of each was written beside it, under the names below.}} Compare them, keep what you want under the original name, then delete the copies: a card’s work that holds one can’t be submitted.
workflow.slots.recoveredCopies.description: HI-2996: after a stale jj slot was recovered: files the user had edited (not yet recorded by jj) had also changed in the update, so Combwork kept the update in the file and wrote the user’s version beside it as a copy (listed under this, as paths). The user compares and deletes the copies; a card can’t be submitted for review while they are in its work.

workflow.slots.recoveredDivergent.defaultMessage: jj also kept commit {commit}, which holds what it recorded of the slot during the recovery. It shows as divergent in jj: once you’ve looked at it, abandon it with jj abandon {commit}.
workflow.slots.recoveredDivergent.description: HI-2996: after a stale jj slot was recovered, jj made a commit of the slot’s files that Combwork couldn’t prove was only what it kept, so it left it (a divergent change in jj). {commit} is its short id. jj abandon is a command: keep it as it is.

workflow.slots.recoveredKeptDeleted.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {You had deleted {files}, but it changed or came back meanwhile, so it was kept.} other {You had deleted {files}, but they changed or came back meanwhile, so they were kept.}}
workflow.slots.recoveredKeptDeleted.description: HI-2996: after a stale jj slot was recovered: files the user had deleted there (not yet recorded by jj) changed in the update or were created again, so Combwork kept them rather than deleting them. {files} lists their paths, joined as a list.

workflow.slots.recoveredPutBack.defaultMessage: {n, plural, =0 {No other file needed putting back.} one {# other file was put back as it was.} other {# other files were put back as they were.}}
workflow.slots.recoveredPutBack.description: HI-2996: after a stale jj slot was recovered, the number of the user’s edited files put back unchanged (nothing to look at for these).

workflow.slots.recoveredTitle.description: HI-2996: the title of the window shown after a stale jj slot ({slot}, its name) was recovered, when the recovery left something for the user to look at: copies it wrote, deleted files it kept, or a commit it kept.

workflow.slots.release.description: A button beside a held slot in the list of slots: asks, then frees it for other work (#1506).

workflow.slots.reviewCopies.description: A read-only row under “Slots and copies”: the setting of Settings → Advanced with this name (as translated there).

workflow.slots.reviewCopiesDesc.defaultMessage: Set in Settings → Advanced, for every project.
workflow.slots.reviewCopiesDesc.description: Under the row “Reviewers review in review copies” of “Slots and copies”: where it is changed.

workflow.slots.saveFailed.description: An error saving a setting under “Slots and copies”.

workflow.slots.setHere.description: Where a slot setting’s value comes from: set in this project.

workflow.slots.setNone.description: Where a slot setting’s value comes from: this project sets it to nothing (no script runs, no files are copied), over the value it would inherit.

workflow.slots.setup.description: A setting under “Slots and copies”: the command Combwork runs in a new slot, and again when its lock files change (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.slots.setupDesc.defaultMessage: Runs in a new slot, and again in a slot whose lock files changed since its last install, e.g. npm ci. Review and check copies run it too.
workflow.slots.setupDesc.description: What the setting “Setup script” does (glossary 2.5: slot, review copy; lock file).

workflow.slots.stale.defaultMessage: Stale: another jj workspace changed it
workflow.slots.stale.description: Beside a jj slot in the list under “Slots and copies” (HI-2869): its files are behind its working-copy commit because another jj workspace rewrote it; it isn’t lent until recovered. “workspace” is jj’s term.

workflow.slots.state.creating.description: A slot’s state in the list under “Slots and copies”.

workflow.slots.state.dirty.description: A slot’s state in the list under “Slots and copies”: it has uncommitted or untracked files, so it isn’t lent until clean.

workflow.slots.state.gone.description: A slot’s state in the list under “Slots and copies”: its folder is gone (Combwork recreates it).

workflow.slots.state.lent.description: A slot’s state in the list under “Slots and copies”: lent to a card or a lane.

workflow.slots.state.ready.description: A slot’s state in the list under “Slots and copies”: free, set up.

workflow.slots.state.removing.description: A slot’s state in the list under “Slots and copies”.

workflow.slots.useNone.description: A button beside a slot setting this project inherits (from the workspace, Combwork’s settings or before 1.0): set it to nothing for this project (no script runs, no files are copied).

workflow.stage.active.description: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Active, was Doing): cards being worked on.

workflow.stage.approved.description: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Approved, was Passed): cards whose work passed review (or your OK) and isn’t merged yet.

workflow.stage.done.description: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Done): cards whose work is merged, or accepted.

workflow.stage.hold.description: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: On Hold): parked cards nobody picks up until the user moves them on.

workflow.stage.merging.description: A stage of the board inside Approved (glossary 2.2: Merging): cards in Combwork's merge queue.

workflow.stage.review.description: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Review): cards waiting for, or in, review.

workflow.stage.todo.description: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Todo): cards not started.

workflow.stageName.control.defaultMessage: The name of {stage} has a character that can’t be shown (a line break or a tab).
workflow.stageName.control.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a stage’s name has a control character. {stage} is the stage’s default name (glossary 2.2).

workflow.stageName.duplicate.defaultMessage: The name of {stage} is already another stage’s name.
workflow.stageName.duplicate.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: two stages would have the same name. {stage} is the default name of the stage renamed (glossary 2.2).

workflow.stageName.empty.defaultMessage: The name of {stage} can’t be empty: remove it to use the default name.
workflow.stageName.empty.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a stage was given an empty name. {stage} is the stage’s default name (glossary 2.2).

workflow.stageName.long.defaultMessage: The name of {stage} is longer than {max, number} characters.
workflow.stageName.long.description: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a stage’s name is too long. {stage} is the stage’s default name (glossary 2.2), {max} the most characters it takes.

workflow.summary.git.pair.defaultMessage: A reviewer agent passes each card, then Combwork’s merge queue merges it once the checks pass on the merged result.
workflow.summary.git.pair.description: What the Pair preset sets up, for a Git project (glossary 2.1: Pair, merge queue).

workflow.summary.git.pairAgent.defaultMessage: A reviewer agent passes each card, then its builder merges it and Combwork checks the work is in the target.
workflow.summary.git.pairAgent.description: What the preset “Pair (the agent merges)” sets up (glossary 2.1: Pair).

workflow.summary.git.solo.defaultMessage: Everyone in the project folder, no review: a card is done once it’s committed.
workflow.summary.git.solo.description: What the Solo preset sets up, for a Git project (glossary 2.1: Solo).

workflow.summary.git.team.defaultMessage: Pair with stricter checks: the unit tests too, a clean install before every merge, and your OK for cards labelled ui or release.
workflow.summary.git.team.description: What the Team preset sets up, for a Git project (glossary 2.1: Team, Pair).

workflow.summary.jj.pair.defaultMessage: A reviewer agent passes each card after the quick checks, then you integrate it yourself.
workflow.summary.jj.pair.description: What the Pair preset sets up, for a project using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799): Combwork never merges under jj.

workflow.summary.jj.solo.defaultMessage: Each card in its own jj workspace, no review: you integrate the work yourself.
workflow.summary.jj.solo.description: What the Solo preset sets up, for a project using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799). Keep jj; a jj workspace is a working folder jj makes.

workflow.summary.jj.team.defaultMessage: A reviewer agent, then you, check each card after the quick checks and the tests, then you integrate it yourself.
workflow.summary.jj.team.description: What the Team preset sets up, for a project using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799): Combwork never merges under jj.

workflow.summary.none.pair.defaultMessage: A reviewer agent checks each card, after the quick checks pass.
workflow.summary.none.pair.description: What the Pair preset sets up, for a project without version control.

workflow.summary.none.solo.defaultMessage: No review: a card is done when its builder submits it.
workflow.summary.none.solo.description: What the Solo preset sets up, for a project without version control.

workflow.summary.none.team.defaultMessage: A reviewer agent, then you, check each card, after the quick checks and the tests pass.
workflow.summary.none.team.description: What the Team preset sets up, for a project without version control.

workflow.unreadable.branch.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.branchedOff.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the commit two lines of work have in common. {a} and {b} are commit ids or branch names.

workflow.unreadable.branchedOffTarget.defaultMessage: where the work branched off its target
workflow.unreadable.branchedOffTarget.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the commit the card's work and the branch it merges into have in common.

workflow.unreadable.cardPathsFiles.defaultMessage: the card's paths: they hold over {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
workflow.unreadable.cardPathsFiles.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the files a card names hold too many files. {n} is the limit.

workflow.unreadable.cardPathsSize.defaultMessage: the card's paths: they hold over {n, number} GB
workflow.unreadable.cardPathsSize.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the files a card names are too large. {n} is a size in gigabytes (GB, of 1024 MB): write the unit as your language does.

workflow.unreadable.change.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (glossary 2.3: change). {from} and {to} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.changeFingerprint.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": what tells a change apart from others (glossary 2.3: change).

workflow.unreadable.commitsOf.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {range} is a Git range of commits, like a1b2c3d..e4f5a6b.

workflow.unreadable.commitsOn.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {target} is a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.commitsSince.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {revision} and {base} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.contains.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {revision} and {target} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.defaultBranch.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the branch work merges into by default. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.deliverables.defaultMessage: the work in {project}: it has over {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
