workflow.unreadable.deliverables.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": a project without version control has too many files to read its work. {project} is a project name, {n} the limit.

workflow.unreadable.files.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the files as they are at a revision. {revision} is a commit id or name.

workflow.unreadable.filesChanged.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {from} and {to} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.folderFor.description: What Combwork couldn't make, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": a working folder (a Git worktree) for a branch. {branch} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.gitFolder.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the repository's .git folder. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.head.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the commit checked out in a folder, or at the tip of a branch. {where} is a folder path or a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.history.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the commits of a branch. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.holdsChange.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": whether the card's change is already in a commit or branch (glossary 2.3: change). {where} is a short commit id or a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.ignored.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the files Git is told to leave out. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.line.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": a Git branch. {branch} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.pathOutside.defaultMessage: the path {path}, which is outside the project
workflow.unreadable.pathOutside.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": a card's path that isn't in its project. {path} is the path.

workflow.unreadable.remoteBehind.defaultMessage: where to start from: {target} has commits that {endpoint} doesn’t (push or pull them first)
workflow.unreadable.remoteBehind.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (HI-1183): the local branch {target} has commits the remote branch it follows (at {endpoint}, an address) lacks, so Combwork won't start a card's work from either.

workflow.unreadable.remoteHead.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (HI-1183): fetching the remote branch {branch} from {endpoint} (a remote's address) failed; {target} is the local branch that follows it. Git's own words follow.

workflow.unreadable.remoteSetup.defaultMessage: the remote branch {target} follows (it must track one, on a remote with a single push address)
workflow.unreadable.remoteSetup.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (HI-1183, “The target branch follows its remote”): the branch on a remote that the target branch {target} tracks; it tracks none, or its remote has several push addresses or none.

workflow.unreadable.replay.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the result of applying a revision's change onto another commit. {revision} and {onto} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.replayedFiles.defaultMessage: the files of the change applied again
workflow.unreadable.replayedFiles.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the result of applying the change again on another commit, to tell whether two revisions are the same change.

workflow.unreadable.reviewers.defaultMessage: whether the reviewers of {card} are still running
workflow.unreadable.reviewers.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (HI-2487): which of the agents reviewing the card are still in the project with their sessions running. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.unreadable.revision.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (glossary 2.3: revision). {revision} is a commit id or name.

workflow.unreadable.revisionIn.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the revision checked out in a folder (glossary 2.3: revision). {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.state.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": whether a merge or rebase is going on in the folder. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.target.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the branch the work merges into. {target} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.uncommitted.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.worktrees.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the Git worktrees of a repository. {folder} is its folder path.

workflow.unreadable.writes.description: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": which files changed in a folder. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.value.commitMessage.branch.defaultMessage: The branch’s own, with no card key or trailers
workflow.value.commitMessage.branch.description: A value of the workflow option “Commit message” (glossary 2.6, G19): the commit takes the message the branch’s commits have (with several, the first one’s subject and each one’s message), never the card’s key or Combwork’s trailers. Trailers: git’s “Key: value” lines at a message’s end.

workflow.value.commitMessage.cw.defaultMessage: Combwork’s: the card’s key and title, with trailers
workflow.value.commitMessage.cw.description: A value of the workflow option “Commit message” (glossary 2.6, G19): the commit is titled with the card’s key and title (HI-12: Fix the login) and ends with Combwork’s trailers (Combwork-Card: HI-12 and others). Trailers: git’s “Key: value” lines at a message’s end.

workflow.value.finish.agentMerges.description: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5).

workflow.value.finish.combworkMerges.description: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5).

workflow.value.finish.committed.description: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5).

workflow.value.finish.notChecked.description: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5).

workflow.value.finish.userIntegrates.description: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5) for a project using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799): Combwork never merges under jj; you bring the reviewed work into its target with jj.

workflow.value.folder.project.description: A value of the workflow option “Where cards are built” (glossary 2.6, G11).

workflow.value.folder.slots.defaultMessage: Each card in its own folder
workflow.value.folder.slots.description: A value of the workflow option “Where cards are built” (glossary 2.6, G11). The folder is a slot, a worktree Combwork lends to the card or its lane (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.value.mergeInstall.always.description: A value of the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch”: before each card’s merge checks.

workflow.value.mergeInstall.alwaysCandid.description: The value “always” of the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch” in a project using jj (HI-2938): before the merge checks on each candidate (the commit Combwork builds for the user to integrate).

workflow.value.mergeInstall.onManifestCh.defaultMessage: When the lock file or manifests change
workflow.value.mergeInstall.onManifestCh.description: A value of the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch”: only when the project’s lock file or package manifests changed (glossary: lock file, as in the G15 value).

workflow.value.okBefore.every.description: A value of the workflow option “Your OK before merging” (glossary 2.6, G10).

workflow.value.okBefore.labels.description: A value of the workflow option “Your OK before merging” (glossary 2.6, G10).

workflow.value.okBefore.never.description: A value of the workflow option “Your OK before merging” (glossary 2.6, G10).

workflow.value.review.agent.description: A value of the workflow option for review (glossary 2.6, G1 and N1).

workflow.value.review.agentThenYou.description: A value of the workflow option for review (glossary 2.6, G1 and N1).

workflow.value.review.none.description: A value of the workflow option “Work is reviewed before it’s merged” (glossary 2.6, G1).

workflow.value.review.noneNone.description: A value of the workflow option “Who checks the work before it’s done”, for a project without version control (glossary 2.6, N1).

workflow.value.review.you.description: A value of the workflow option for review: you review (glossary 2.6, G1 and N1).

workflow.value.reviewerMode.lane.description: A value of the workflow option “Reviewers” (glossary 2.6, G17): each lane has its own reviewer agent.

workflow.value.reviewerMode.pool.description: A value of the workflow option “Reviewers” (glossary 2.6, G17): lanes share a pool of reviewer agents, each card going to the next free one.

workflow.value.sameness.change.description: A value of the workflow option “A pass survives a clean rebase” (glossary 2.6, G4).

workflow.value.sameness.exact.description: A value of the workflow option “A pass survives a clean rebase” (glossary 2.6, G4).

workflow.value.style.merge.description: A value of the workflow option “Merge style” (glossary 2.6, G6).

workflow.value.style.rebase.description: A value of the workflow option “Merge style” (glossary 2.6, G6; #1184): Combwork’s merge queue rebases the card’s commits onto the target branch and moves the branch forward to them, so the history stays linear, with no merge commit.

workflow.value.style.squash.description: A value of the workflow option “Merge style” (glossary 2.6, G6).

workflow.why.commitMessage.defaultMessage: Card titles can name people and details a public history shouldn’t keep; choose Combwork’s for the card’s key, linking each merge to its card.
workflow.why.commitMessage.description: Why the presets set “Commit message” to the branch’s own (HI-1997), and what choosing Combwork’s (the card’s key and title, with trailers) gives instead.

workflow.why.dependenciesDone.defaultMessage: It’s cheap, and no card is built on work that isn’t in yet.
workflow.why.dependenciesDone.description: Why every preset turns on “Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged” (or done).

workflow.why.excluded.defaultMessage: Dependencies and build output aren’t part of what a card delivers.
workflow.why.excluded.description: Why the presets leave node_modules and .venv out of “What the work is” (no version control).

workflow.why.finish.defaultMessage: Merged through Combwork’s queue, red work never reaches the target branch; working solo, a card is done once it’s committed.
workflow.why.finish.description: Why the presets set “Who merges” as they do (glossary 2.1: merge queue).

workflow.why.focusedTests.defaultMessage: Each card’s own tests on the merged result catch what its change breaks there, without running every test for every card.
workflow.why.focusedTests.description: Why Team turns on “Each card’s focused tests pass on the merged result” when the project has the command that runs them.

workflow.why.folder.defaultMessage: Pairs and teams build in parallel, each card apart from the others.
workflow.why.folder.description: Why the presets set “Where cards are built” as they do (Solo: the project folder).

workflow.why.followRemote.defaultMessage: Following a remote reaches it and its sign-in before every merge, so it stays yours unless you turn it on.
workflow.why.followRemote.description: Why the presets leave “The target branch follows its remote” off.

workflow.why.identity.defaultMessage: Commits name the project’s identity, whoever’s computer made them.
workflow.why.identity.description: Why Pair and Team turn on “Commits use the project’s identity”.

workflow.why.maxAgents.defaultMessage: Each preset is for a team of its size (one agent solo, a builder and a reviewer as a pair), so the Assistant never adds agents you didn’t plan for.
workflow.why.maxAgents.description: Why the presets set “Maximum agents” as they do (Solo: 1; Pair: 2; Team: 12).

workflow.why.mergeChecks.defaultMessage: The checks run on the work as it will be once merged, not only as it was built.
workflow.why.mergeChecks.description: Why the presets set “Checks pass on the merged result” when Combwork merges.

workflow.why.mergeInstall.defaultMessage: A clean install before every merge catches a dependency that only worked on the builder’s machine.
workflow.why.mergeInstall.description: Why Team installs dependencies from scratch before every merge.

workflow.why.noSelfReview.defaultMessage: A builder never passes its own work.
workflow.why.noSelfReview.description: Why the presets turn on “Nobody reviews their own work” wherever there is a reviewer.

workflow.why.okBefore.defaultMessage: Some work needs your eyes before it ships, such as screenshots and release steps.
workflow.why.okBefore.description: Why Team asks for your OK on cards labelled ui or release.

workflow.why.preChecks.defaultMessage: Cheap checks before review catch most of the rounds that would be lost, and a team adds its tests.
workflow.why.preChecks.description: Why the presets set “Checks pass before review” as they do (Pair: the quick checks; Team: the tests too).

workflow.why.pushTarget.defaultMessage: Pushing reaches your remote and its sign-in, so it stays yours unless you turn it on.
workflow.why.pushTarget.description: Why the presets leave “Push the target branch after merging” off.

workflow.why.review.defaultMessage: A pair exists to review: a second agent catches what the builder missed, while working solo you read the card’s work yourself.
workflow.why.review.description: Why the presets set “Work is reviewed before it’s merged” as they do (Solo: no review; Pair and Team: a reviewer agent).

workflow.why.reviewerMode.defaultMessage: One reviewer per lane keeps the work with a reviewer who has seen its earlier rounds; a shared pool suits a large team.
workflow.why.reviewerMode.description: Why Pair and Team set “Reviewers” to One per lane (glossary 2.6, G17; glossary: lane, pool).

workflow.why.reviewers.defaultMessage: One reviewer is enough for most work; a second doubles the cost.
workflow.why.reviewers.description: Why the presets set “Reviewers per card” to 1.

workflow.why.sameness.defaultMessage: A clean rebase doesn’t change what was reviewed, so the pass still counts.
workflow.why.sameness.description: Why every preset sets “A pass survives a clean rebase” to Same change.

workflow.why.sharedFolderWarning.defaultMessage: In a shared folder, one agent’s commit can take in another’s half-done files.
workflow.why.sharedFolderWarning.description: Why Solo turns on “Warn when a commit includes another agent’s files”.

workflow.why.slotsUpToDate.defaultMessage: Each card starts from the latest work, so no card is built on an old copy of the target branch.
workflow.why.slotsUpToDate.description: Why Pair and Team turn on “Slots are brought up to date before each card” (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.why.stopOwnRuns.defaultMessage: A run left going would keep changing or testing the work under review.
workflow.why.stopOwnRuns.description: Why Pair and Team turn on “Agents stop what they started before review”.

workflow.why.strict.defaultMessage: The merge queue tests the merged result anyway, so this mostly changes the history’s shape.
workflow.why.strict.description: Why the presets leave “Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges” off.

workflow.why.style.defaultMessage: A merge commit keeps each card’s own commits, as Combwork has always merged.
workflow.why.style.description: Why the presets set “Merge style” to Merge commit.

workflow.why.target.defaultMessage: Finished work goes to the repository’s default branch; working solo, to the branch the project is on.
workflow.why.target.description: Why the presets set “Work merges into” as they do.
